November 19, 2026 
Respected Sir/Madam, 
 
Subject: Intimation under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Order passed by the Appellate Tribunal for 
Electricity, New Delhi in the matter relating to Beta Wind Farm Private Limited, a 
material subsidiary of the Company 
 
In furtherance to our earlier intimation dated October 04, 2023 with regard to pendency 
of litigations or disputes (if any), we wish to inform you that the Appellate Tribunal for 
Electricity (APTEL), vide its judgment dated November 17, 2026, has pronounced its order 
in the appeals filed by various wind power generators, including Beta Wind Farm Private 
Limited (Beta), a material subsidiary of the Company. 
 
The order is favourable to Beta and entitles Beta to receive payment for the energy 
supplied beyond the normative CUF, together with applicable interest, in accordance with 
the terms of the PPA. 
 
The details/disclosures in respect of the order, as required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI 
Listing Regulations, read with Schedule III thereto and SEBI Master Circular dated 
January 30, 2026, are provided in the enclosed Annexure-I 
 
We request you to take the same on your records. 
 
Thanking you,  
Yours faithfully, 
 
For Orient Green Power Company Limited 
 
 
 
G. Srinivasa Ramanujan  
Company Secretary & Compliance Officer 
 
The BSE Limited                                        
Corporate Relations Department,                     
P.J. Towers, 
Dalal Street, 
Mumbai-400 001. 
Scrip Code: 533263 
 
The National Stock Exchange  
of India Limited 
Department of Corporate Services, 
Exchange Plaza, 5th Floor,  
Bandra-Kurla Complex, 
Mumbai-400 051. 
Scrip Code:  GREENPOWER 

 
 
 
 
Annexure – I 
 
Information as required under Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and SEBI Master Circular No.  
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026  dated January 30, 2026 
 
S.No Particulars Details 
1 Name of the Opposing party Southern Power Distribution Company 
of Andhra Pradesh Limited (APSPDCL) 
2 Court / Tribunal / Agency Appellate Tribunal for Electricity 
(APTEL) 
3 Brief details of litigation The appeal was filed by Beta Wind Farm 
Private Limited, a material subsidiary of 
the Company(Beta), challenging the 
order passed by the Andhra Pradesh 
Electricity Regulatory Commission 
(APERC) concerning the restriction of 
payment for wind energy supplied 
beyond the normative Capacity 
Utilisation Factor (CUF). Beta prayed 
for release of Rs. 5.93 crore withheld by 
APSPCDL along with interest as per the 
Power Purchase Agreement(PPA).  
4 Expected financial implications, if 
any 
Beta is expected to receive about              
Rs. 12.98 crore which include Rs. 5.93 
crore of amounts withheld and Rs. 7.05 
crore of interest calculated till October 
31, 2026. 
5 Quantum of claims, if any Rs. 5.93 Crores withheld by APSPCDL 
along with interest as per the power 
purchase agreement till the date of 
payment. 
6 In the event of settlement of the 
proceedings, details of such 
settlement including - terms of the 
settlement, compensation/penalty 
paid (if any) and impact of such 
settlement on the financial position of 
the listed entity.  
 
APTEL after hearings passed an order 
on November 17, 2026, setting aside the 
impugned order of APERC and directed 
APSPDCL to release the withheld 
amount along with interest as per the 
terms of PPA.

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Sub: Disclosure under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 
 
Pursuant to the provisions of regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘Listing Regulations’), we hereby 
submit the disclosure regarding the order received from Office of the 
Commissioner (Appeals), Central Goods & Services Tax Appeals 
Commissionerate, Jammu , pertaining to Excise Duty Demand of Rs. 5,50,14,380/-
under the J&K area-based exemption scheme (Notification No. 56/2002-CE) 
claimed by the Company’s Samba unit. 
  
The details of the above order as required under Regulation 30 of Listing 
Regulations are given below: 
 
Sr. 
No. 
Particulars Details 
1 Name of the Authority Office of the Commissioner (Appeals), 
Central Goods & Services Tax Appeals 
Commissionerate, Jammu 
2 Nature and details of the 
action(s) 
The Company had received Excise Duty 
Demand JNK-CE-APP-08-2026-27 dated 
17-11-2026 amounting to Rs. 5,50,14,380/-
along with interest under Section 11AA/ 
11AB of the Central Excise Act 1944 on 
18th November 2026. 
 
The demand related to refund claims 

 
 
 
under the J&K area-based exemption 
(Notification No. 56/2002-CE) for our 
Samba unit. 
3 Date of receipt of 
communication from the 
authority 
18th November, 2026  
4 Details of the violation(s) / 
contravention(s) committed or 
alleged to be committed; 
The Department has alleged that the 
Company had availed excess refund 
under the J&K area-based exemption 
scheme (Notification No. 56/2002-CE) 
without final approval of the special rate 
of value addition. The Department 
considered only the standard 36% value 
addition and treated the excess refund 
claimed by the Company—based on a 
higher special rate—as inadmissible, 
leading to the issuance of demand. 
 
5 Impact on financial, 
operational, or other activities 
of the listed entity, quantifiable 
in monetary terms to the extent 
possible. 
  
There is no material impact on financials, 
operations or other activities of the 
Company due to the order of tax 
payable. This Order is currently 
appealable, the company will file an 
appeal with CESTAT Chandigarh 
 
Kindly take the above information on record. 
 
Thanking You. 
 
Yours faithfully, 
 
FOR KOKUYO CAMLIN LIMITED 
 
 
 
SATISH VEERAPPA  
MANAGING DIRECTOR

Dear Sir: 
 
Sub: Initiation of investigation and interim measures by U.S. Customs and Border Protection Office 
Ref:  Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of th e Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (the Regulations)  
 
Pursuant to the Regulation 30 of the Regulations, we inform you that Atul USA Inc, a wholly-owned 
subsidiary entity of the Company has received a noti ce from U.S. Customs and Border Protection Office 
under the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015, commonly referred as the Enforcement 
and Protect Act (EAPA) for alleged evasion of antidumping duty (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) on 
imports by it. The details as required under the Regulations are as under: 
 
Name of the authority  U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) 
Nature and details of the action(s) taken,  
initiated or order(s) passed; 
CBP has initiated an investigation based on the suspicion 
that Chinese 2,4-Dichlorophen oxyacetic Acid (2,4-D) and 
its derivatives were transhipped through India to the USA 
warranting higher AD and CV D. The investigation is 
initiated against Atul USA Inc to ascertain alleged evasion 
of AD and CVD on 2,4-D and its derivatives.  As an interim 
measure, CBP has suspended the liquidation of each 
unliquidated entry of such covered merchandise that 
entered into the USA after August 11, 2026 or as permitted 
by law. CBP may also take additional measures necessary 
to protect the revenue of the United States. 
Date of receipt of direction or order,  
including any ad-interim or interim orders, 
or any other communication from the 
authority;  
The copy of the public version of the notice was received by 
us on November 18, 2026 at 21:50 IST. 
Details of the violation(s) | contravention(s) 
committed or alleged to be committed; 
Alleged evasion of AD and CVD  

  
 
Impact on financial, operation or other  
activities of the listed entity, quantifiable in 
monetary terms to the extent possible 
Prima facie, the Company denies the allegation. The impact 
is uncertain at this stage. It has engaged US based lawyers 
to seek advice and guidance in the matter.   
Any other relevant information None.  
 
We request you to inform the members of the exchange accordingly.  
 
Thank you,  
 
Yours faithfully, 
 
For Atul Limited 
 
 
Lalit Patni 
Company Secretary and 
Chief Compliance Officer

Sub: Notice for non-compliance with Regulation 38 of SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure 
This is with reference to Regulation 38 of the Listing Regulations, according to which the listed entity is 
required to comply with Minimum Public Shareholding as specified in Rule 19(2) and 19A of the Securities 
Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957. It has been observed that your Company is non-compliant with the said 
requirement for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Your attention is drawn towards SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 
Exchange is required to levy fine on the non-compliant listed entity, and such fine shall continue to be 
imposed till the date of achieving Compliance. In view of the identified non-compliance, the total fine 
payable by your Company and the particulars about manner in which the fine shall be remitted to the 
Exchange is enclosed as Annexure.
You are hereby notified to ensure Compliance with respective regulation and/or make the payment of fine 
levied, failing which the Exchange would initiate action of freezing the entire Shareholding of the Promoter 
and Promoter Group in the Company as per SEBI Master Circular, 
Further you are requested to intimate the Promoters, Promoter Group and Directors of your Company that 
they shall not hold any new position as director in any other listed entity till the date of compliance with 
Regulation 38 of the Listing Regulations.
Upon receipt of this review notice, the company may file the waiver request. Below are the parameters for 
filing the application for waiver: 
a) Waiver applications sent via mail is not considered. The Company is requested to submit waiver  
application on the below mentioned path:
NEAPS>>Compliance>>Fine Waiver>>Waiver Request
b) Detailed submission indicating reasons for waiver, mentioning whether it intends to seek personal 
hearing before the concerned Committee.
c) Further, compliance is a pre-requisite for applying for waiver. Thus, waiver application of the 
non-complied Companies will not be processed without achieving the compliance.
d) In case the Company is non-compliant under multiple regulations, the Company is advised to file 
a single application mentioning the details of all the respective regulations and quarters for which 
the Company intends to apply for waiver.


e) Non-refundable Processing fees for an amount of Rs.10,000 plus 18% GST to be paid to the 
designated Exchange, (as segregated between the Exchanges as per the policy for waiver of fines) 
only if the fine amount is more than Rs. 5,000/-.
However, before filing an application for waiver of fines, you are requested to refer to the below policy 
Policy on processing of waiver application: 
https://nsearchives.nseindia.com//web/circular/2026-
01/Policy_for_waiver_of_fines_Final1_20260113193131.pdf
Further your Company is requested to provide clarification to this notice of the Exchange on or before
Thursday, November 26, 2026 or else action as per above mentioned SEBI Circular may be initiated against 
the Company.
Yours faithfully,
For National Stock Exchange of India Limited

of NCT of Delhi (‘Appellate Authority’), disposing of the appeal filed by the Company (‘ Appellate 
Order’). The Order was received by the Company on November 20, 2026 at 13:30 hours.

deposit of INR 36,15,950/- (refundable).

compliance; and

Dear Sirs, 
 
In accordance with Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements 
Regulations, 2015, this is to inform you that the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai,  
(“NCLT”) vide an order dated November 20, 2026 (“Order”) has approved the Scheme.

information and records. The certified copy of the Order shall be obtained in due course.

ORDER 
 
1. The present Company Scheme Petition has been filed in the matter 
of the Scheme of Amalgamation between Everblue Apparel 
Limited (hereinafter referred to as ‘EBAL’ or the ‘Transferor 
Company’ or ‘First Petitioner Company’) with Raymond Limited 
(hereinafter referred to as ‘RL’ or the ‘Transferee Company’ or 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 3  
 
‘Second Petitioner Company’). [The First Petitioner Company 
and the Second Petitioner Company are collectively referred to as 
“the Petitioner Companies”] and their respective shareholders and 
creditors (hereinafter referred to as “Scheme”) under Sections 230 
to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 
read with Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and 
Amalgamations) Rules, 2016. 
 
2. The First Petitioner Company bearing CIN: 
U72900MH2000PLC124912 was incorporated under the 
provisions of the Companies Act, 1956 on 14.03.2000 under the 
name ‘Raymond Infotech Limited’. Subsequently, on 
16.02.2004, the name of the First Petitioner Company was changed 
to ‘Everblue Apparel Limited’. Having its registered office at 
New Hind House, Narottam Morarjee, Ballard Estate, Mumbai, 
Maharashtra, India, 400001. It is engaged in the business of 
converting fabrics into readymade garments on contractual basis. 
The First Petitioner Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the 
Second Petitioner Company. 
3. The Second Petitioner Company, bearing CIN: 
L17117MH1925PLC001208, was incorporated under the 
provisions of the Indian Companies Act, 1913, on 10.09.1925, 
under the name ‘The Raymond Woollen Mills Limited’. 
Subsequently, on 31.03.1995, the name of the Second Petitioner 
Company was changed to ‘Raymond Limited’. Its registered office 
is at Plot No 156/h. No. 2, Village Zadgaon, Ratnagiri – 415612, 
Maharashtra, India. It is engaged in the manufacture of denim 
fabric, denim garmenting, and the engineering and aerospace 
business through joint ventures and subsidiary companies. 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 4  
 
4. The registered offices of the Petitioner Companies are located in 
Maharashtra and fall within the territorial jurisdiction of the 
Tribunal. 
5. The Board of Directors of the First Petitioner Company and the 
Second Petitioner Company, at their respective board meetings 
held on 23.01.2026 and 27.01.2026, have approved the Scheme. 
The Appointed Date fixed under the Scheme is 01.04.2026.  
6. The equity shares of the Second Petitioner Company are listed on 
the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock 
Exchange of India Limited (NSE). 
7. The Rationale for the proposed Scheme is as under: 
“To enable simplified structure and greater management focus 
on the business, it is imperative for the Transferor Company to 
be merged into the Transferee Company.  
The proposed amalgamation would achieve the following 
benefits: 
(i) Simplification of overall group structure by fully integrating 
EBAL’s garmenting operations directly within RL and 
creating efficiencies through amalgamation; 
(ii) Optimal utilization of existing resources through 
consolidation of operations into a single legal entity; 
(iii) Provide an opportunity to leverage and pool resources of the 
respective companies; 
(iv) Derive operational and financial synergies through prudent 
financial management and cost reduction; and 
(v) Better administration, reduction / rationalization in costs, 
focused operational efforts and elimination of duplication.  
 
Therefore, the Board of Directors of the companies involved 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 5  
 
in the Scheme have proposed amalgamation of EBAL with RL 
and their respective shareholders under the provisions of 
Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013.” 
 
8. Consideration under the scheme is as under: - 
“12 CONSIDERATION: 
12.1 The entire issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share 
capital of Transferor Company is held by the Transferee 
Company and/ or its nominee(s). Upon the Scheme becoming 
effective, no shares of the Transferee Company shall be allotted 
in lieu or exchange of the holding of equity shares in Transferor 
Company and the entire issued, subscribed and paid up share 
capital of the Transferor Company shall stand automatically 
cancelled. 
12.2 Upon the Scheme becoming effective, the share 
certificates, if any, and/or the shares in electronic form or 
physical form as the case may be, representing the equity 
shares held by the Transferee Company in the Transferor 
Company shall be deemed to be cancelled without any further 
act or deed.” 
9. The Petitioner Companies have inter alia submitted the following 
documents: - 
a. Master data from MCA, MOA & AOA along with the 
Certificate of Incorporation of the Petitioner Companies. 
b. Audited Financials Statement as on 31.03.2026. 
c. Board Resolution dated 23 January 2026 and 27 January 
2026 by First Petitioner Company and Second Petitioner 
Company approving the proposed Scheme; 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 6  
 
d. Certificate issued by the Statutory Auditors confirming the 
accounting treatment proposed in the Scheme of the 
Petitioner Companies. 
10. The Petitioner Companies have complied with all requirements as 
per the directions of this Tribunal vide order dated 19.06.2026 
passed in C.A.(CAA) No. 96/MB/2026, and have filed the 
necessary affidavits of compliance before this Tribunal. Moreover, 
the Petitioner Companies have undertaken to comply with all 
statutory requirements, if any, as may be required under the 
Companies Act, 2013, and the Rules made thereunder. 
11. The Petitioner Companies have submitted that notices under 
Section 230(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 were duly served upon 
the regulatory authorities, as directed by this Adjudicating 
Authority vide order dated 19.06.2026, and that an affidavit of 
service dated 23.07.2026 has been filed on record, thereby 
evidencing the same. 
12. The Regional Director, Western Region I, has filed his report dated 
16.10.2026 (‘RD Report I’), making certain observations therein. 
The Petitioner Companies have filed their affidavit in rejoinder to 
the Regional Director’s report on 19.10.2026 and have 
submitted/undertaken that: 
i) The interests of the creditors and employees will remain 
protected. 
ii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with sections 230 to 232 
of the Companies Act, 2013. Where the Transferor company is 
dissolved, the fee and stamp duty paid by the Transferor 
company on its authorised capital shall be set off against the fees 
and stamp duty payable by the Transferee company on its 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 7  
 
authorised capital subsequent to the merger, and the Transferor 
company will pay the difference in fees and stamp duty. 
iii) The Transferee Company shall, in addition to complying with 
Accounting Standard-14 or Ind AS-103, pass such accounting 
entries as may be necessary in connection with the Scheme to 
ensure compliance with other applicable Accounting Standards, 
including AS-5 and Ind AS-8. 
iv) The approval of the Scheme by this Tribunal shall not preclude 
the concerned authorities from examining any issues arising after 
the Scheme takes effect. Their decisions shall be binding on the 
Petitioner Companies. 
v) The Scheme enclosed with the Company Application and the 
Company Petition are one and the same, and there is no 
discrepancy or change. 
vi) The Petitioner Companies have complied with Section 230(5) of 
the Companies Act, 2013 and have served the requisite notices 
on all concerned authorities likely to be affected by the present 
scheme. 
vii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with all applicable 
provisions of the Income-tax Act and the requirements of the 
GST authorities. 
viii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the directions 
of the sectoral regulatory authorities, if any. 
ix) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the requirements 
clarified vide Circular No. F. No. 7/12/2019/CL-I, dated 
21.08.2019, issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. 
x) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the provisions of 
Section 2(1B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, and with the 
directions issued by this Tribunal. 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 8  
 
xi) Without prejudice, the Transferor Company and the Transferee 
Company have filed Form BEN-2 with the Registrar of 
Companies and have complied with the provisions of Section 90 
of the Companies Act, 2013, read with Rule 2(1)(h) of the 
Companies (Significant Beneficial Owners) Rules, 2018. 
13. The Regional Director, Western Region II, has filed his report 
dated 21.10.2026 (‘RD Report II’), making certain observations 
therein. The Petitioner Companies have filed their affidavit in 
rejoinder to the Regional Director’s report on 22.10.2026 and have 
submitted/undertaken that: 
i) In addition to compliance of IND-AS 103 for accounting 
treatment, the Petitioner Companies shall pass such accounting 
entries as may be necessary in connection with the Scheme to 
comply with other applicable accounting standards, as 
applicable. 
ii) The Scheme enclosed to the Company Application and the 
Company Petition are one and the same, and there is no 
discrepancy, or no change is made. 
iii) The Petitioner Companies have complied with the provisions of 
Section 230(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 and have served the 
requisite notices on all concerned authorities likely to be affected 
by the present scheme. 
iv) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the directions of the 
sectoral regulatory authorities, if any. 
v) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the I.T. Department 
and the GST Department, as required. 
vi) The interests of the creditors and employees would remain 
protected. 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 9  
 
vii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the provisions of 
Section 2 (1B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 and the directions 
passed by this Tribunal. 
viii) The Petitioner Companies have filed a similar application before 
the Regional Director, Western Region – I and have submitted 
appropriate responses to its report vide an Affidavit dated 
19.10.2026. 
ix) The Scheme provides for the merger of a wholly owned 
subsidiary with its holding company; the requirement to obtain 
the No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Stock Exchanges 
is not applicable to the present Scheme.   
14. The Official Liquidator has filed his report dated 5th October 2026. 
The Transferor Company has stated that it has no further 
submissions to make in respect of the report. The contents of the 
report are taken on record. 
15. During the course of the hearing, the Second Petitioner Company 
received a copy of a letter dated 07.10.2026 from the State Tax 
Officer, Jammu & Kashmir. It is hereby clarified that any GST or 
state tax-related issue pending or arising out of this Scheme will be 
addressed in accordance with law, and that the rights of the State 
Tax Officer would remain intact to initiate appropriate proceedings 
for assessment of tax due or any other proceedings in relation 
thereto or arising therefrom against the Petitioner Companies at any 
future date, and that these rights would not be adversely affected in 
view of the sanctioning of the Scheme. 
16. No objections have been received from any other statutory or 
regulatory authority. Accordingly, the Scheme is deemed to be 
unopposed.  

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 10  
 
17. We have perused the submissions made by the Petitioner 
Companies and the reports submitted by the Regional Director 
(RD) and the Official Liquidator (OL). The Petitioner Companies 
have undertaken to comply with all the undertakings given in their 
replies to the observations of the RD. 
18. From the material on record, the Scheme appears to be fair and 
reasonable, does not violate any provisions of law, and is not 
contrary to public policy, as no objection has so far been received 
from any other authority, creditors, members, or any other 
stakeholders. 
19. Since all the requisite statutory compliances have been fulfilled, the 
Company Petition bearing C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in 
C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 is made absolute in terms of the prayer 
clauses of the said Company Scheme Petition. It shall be binding 
on the Petitioner Companies and all concerned, including their 
respective Shareholders, Creditors, Employees, and/or any other 
stakeholders. 
20. The Transferor Company is dissolved without winding up. 
21. The Income Tax Department will be at liberty to examine the 
aspects relating to any tax payable as a result of this scheme. If it is 
found that the scheme ultimately results in tax avoidance under the 
provisions of the Income Tax Act, it shall be open to the Income 
Tax authorities to take such necessary action as may be possible 
under the Income Tax Law. 
22. Needless to say, all liabilities accruing in the transferor company 
shall be transferred to the Transferee Company; however, the 
liabilities in respect of offences committed under this Act by the 
officers in default of the transferor company prior to its merger, 
amalgamation or acquisition shall continue after such merger, 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 11  
 
amalgamation or acquisition as provided in Section 240 of the 
Companies Act, 2013. 
23. The Petitioner Companies are directed to file a copy of this Order 
and a copy of the Scheme with the concerned Registrar of 
Companies electronically, along with E-Form INC-28, within 30 
days from the date of receipt of the Order by the Petitioner 
Companies. 
24. All the employees of the Transferor Company in service on the date 
immediately preceding the date on which the Scheme takes effect, 
i.e., the effective Date, shall become the employees of the 
Transferee Company on such date, without any break or 
interruption in service, and upon terms and conditions not less 
favourable than those subsisting in the concerned Transferor 
Companies on the said date. 
25. The Petitioner Companies shall lodge a copy of this order and the 
Scheme, duly authenticated by the Deputy Registrar/Assistant 
Registrar of this Tribunal, with the concerned Superintendent of 
Stamps for the purpose of adjudication of stamp duty, if any, 
payable on the same within 60 days from the date of receipt of the 
copy of the order. 
26. The present Company Scheme Petition, i.e. 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026, is allowed 
and disposed of, ordered accordingly. 
 
 
 Sd/- Sd/- 
Sh. Prabhat Kumar               Sh. Sushil Mahadeorao Kochey 
Member (Technical) Member (Judicial)

business through joint ventures and subsidiary companies. 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 4  
 
4. The registered offices of the Petitioner Companies are located in 
Maharashtra and fall within the territorial jurisdiction of the 
Tribunal. 
5. The Board of Directors of the First Petitioner Company and the 
Second Petitioner Company, at their respective board meetings 
held on 23.01.2026 and 27.01.2026, have approved the Scheme. 
The Appointed Date fixed under the Scheme is 01.04.2026.  
6. The equity shares of the Second Petitioner Company are listed on 
the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock 
Exchange of India Limited (NSE). 
7. The Rationale for the proposed Scheme is as under: 
“To enable simplified structure and greater management focus 
on the business, it is imperative for the Transferor Company to 
be merged into the Transferee Company.  
The proposed amalgamation would achieve the following 
benefits: 
(i) Simplification of overall group structure by fully integrating 
EBAL’s garmenting operations directly within RL and 
creating efficiencies through amalgamation; 
(ii) Optimal utilization of existing resources through 
consolidation of operations into a single legal entity; 
(iii) Provide an opportunity to leverage and pool resources of the 
respective companies; 
(iv) Derive operational and financial synergies through prudent 
financial management and cost reduction; and 
(v) Better administration, reduction / rationalization in costs, 
focused operational efforts and elimination of duplication.  
 
Therefore, the Board of Directors of the companies involved 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 5  
 
in the Scheme have proposed amalgamation of EBAL with RL 
and their respective shareholders under the provisions of 
Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013.” 
 
8. Consideration under the scheme is as under: - 
“12 CONSIDERATION: 
12.1 The entire issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share 
capital of Transferor Company is held by the Transferee 
Company and/ or its nominee(s). Upon the Scheme becoming 
effective, no shares of the Transferee Company shall be allotted 
in lieu or exchange of the holding of equity shares in Transferor 
Company and the entire issued, subscribed and paid up share 
capital of the Transferor Company shall stand automatically 
cancelled. 
12.2 Upon the Scheme becoming effective, the share 
certificates, if any, and/or the shares in electronic form or 
physical form as the case may be, representing the equity 
shares held by the Transferee Company in the Transferor 
Company shall be deemed to be cancelled without any further 
act or deed.” 
9. The Petitioner Companies have inter alia submitted the following 
documents: - 
a. Master data from MCA, MOA & AOA along with the 
Certificate of Incorporation of the Petitioner Companies. 
b. Audited Financials Statement as on 31.03.2026. 
c. Board Resolution dated 23 January 2026 and 27 January 
2026 by First Petitioner Company and Second Petitioner 
Company approving the proposed Scheme; 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 6  
 
d. Certificate issued by the Statutory Auditors confirming the 
accounting treatment proposed in the Scheme of the 
Petitioner Companies. 
10. The Petitioner Companies have complied with all requirements as 
per the directions of this Tribunal vide order dated 19.06.2026 
passed in C.A.(CAA) No. 96/MB/2026, and have filed the 
necessary affidavits of compliance before this Tribunal. Moreover, 
the Petitioner Companies have undertaken to comply with all 
statutory requirements, if any, as may be required under the 
Companies Act, 2013, and the Rules made thereunder. 
11. The Petitioner Companies have submitted that notices under 
Section 230(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 were duly served upon 
the regulatory authorities, as directed by this Adjudicating 
Authority vide order dated 19.06.2026, and that an affidavit of 
service dated 23.07.2026 has been filed on record, thereby 
evidencing the same. 
12. The Regional Director, Western Region I, has filed his report dated 
16.10.2026 (‘RD Report I’), making certain observations therein. 
The Petitioner Companies have filed their affidavit in rejoinder to 
the Regional Director’s report on 19.10.2026 and have 
submitted/undertaken that: 
i) The interests of the creditors and employees will remain 
protected. 
ii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with sections 230 to 232 
of the Companies Act, 2013. Where the Transferor company is 
dissolved, the fee and stamp duty paid by the Transferor 
company on its authorised capital shall be set off against the fees 
and stamp duty payable by the Transferee company on its 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 7  
 
authorised capital subsequent to the merger, and the Transferor 
company will pay the difference in fees and stamp duty. 
iii) The Transferee Company shall, in addition to complying with 
Accounting Standard-14 or Ind AS-103, pass such accounting 
entries as may be necessary in connection with the Scheme to 
ensure compliance with other applicable Accounting Standards, 
including AS-5 and Ind AS-8. 
iv) The approval of the Scheme by this Tribunal shall not preclude 
the concerned authorities from examining any issues arising after 
the Scheme takes effect. Their decisions shall be binding on the 
Petitioner Companies. 
v) The Scheme enclosed with the Company Application and the 
Company Petition are one and the same, and there is no 
discrepancy or change. 
vi) The Petitioner Companies have complied with Section 230(5) of 
the Companies Act, 2013 and have served the requisite notices 
on all concerned authorities likely to be affected by the present 
scheme. 
vii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with all applicable 
provisions of the Income-tax Act and the requirements of the 
GST authorities. 
viii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the directions 
of the sectoral regulatory authorities, if any. 
ix) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the requirements 
clarified vide Circular No. F. No. 7/12/2019/CL-I, dated 
21.08.2019, issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. 
x) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the provisions of 
Section 2(1B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, and with the 
directions issued by this Tribunal. 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 8  
 
xi) Without prejudice, the Transferor Company and the Transferee 
Company have filed Form BEN-2 with the Registrar of 
Companies and have complied with the provisions of Section 90 
of the Companies Act, 2013, read with Rule 2(1)(h) of the 
Companies (Significant Beneficial Owners) Rules, 2018. 
13. The Regional Director, Western Region II, has filed his report 
dated 21.10.2026 (‘RD Report II’), making certain observations 
therein. The Petitioner Companies have filed their affidavit in 
rejoinder to the Regional Director’s report on 22.10.2026 and have 
submitted/undertaken that: 
i) In addition to compliance of IND-AS 103 for accounting 
treatment, the Petitioner Companies shall pass such accounting 
entries as may be necessary in connection with the Scheme to 
comply with other applicable accounting standards, as 
applicable. 
ii) The Scheme enclosed to the Company Application and the 
Company Petition are one and the same, and there is no 
discrepancy, or no change is made. 
iii) The Petitioner Companies have complied with the provisions of 
Section 230(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 and have served the 
requisite notices on all concerned authorities likely to be affected 
by the present scheme. 
iv) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the directions of the 
sectoral regulatory authorities, if any. 
v) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the I.T. Department 
and the GST Department, as required. 
vi) The interests of the creditors and employees would remain 
protected. 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 9  
 
vii) The Petitioner Companies shall comply with the provisions of 
Section 2 (1B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 and the directions 
passed by this Tribunal. 
viii) The Petitioner Companies have filed a similar application before 
the Regional Director, Western Region – I and have submitted 
appropriate responses to its report vide an Affidavit dated 
19.10.2026. 
ix) The Scheme provides for the merger of a wholly owned 
subsidiary with its holding company; the requirement to obtain 
the No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Stock Exchanges 
is not applicable to the present Scheme.   
14. The Official Liquidator has filed his report dated 5th October 2026. 
The Transferor Company has stated that it has no further 
submissions to make in respect of the report. The contents of the 
report are taken on record. 
15. During the course of the hearing, the Second Petitioner Company 
received a copy of a letter dated 07.10.2026 from the State Tax 
Officer, Jammu & Kashmir. It is hereby clarified that any GST or 
state tax-related issue pending or arising out of this Scheme will be 
addressed in accordance with law, and that the rights of the State 
Tax Officer would remain intact to initiate appropriate proceedings 
for assessment of tax due or any other proceedings in relation 
thereto or arising therefrom against the Petitioner Companies at any 
future date, and that these rights would not be adversely affected in 
view of the sanctioning of the Scheme. 
16. No objections have been received from any other statutory or 
regulatory authority. Accordingly, the Scheme is deemed to be 
unopposed.  

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 10  
 
17. We have perused the submissions made by the Petitioner 
Companies and the reports submitted by the Regional Director 
(RD) and the Official Liquidator (OL). The Petitioner Companies 
have undertaken to comply with all the undertakings given in their 
replies to the observations of the RD. 
18. From the material on record, the Scheme appears to be fair and 
reasonable, does not violate any provisions of law, and is not 
contrary to public policy, as no objection has so far been received 
from any other authority, creditors, members, or any other 
stakeholders. 
19. Since all the requisite statutory compliances have been fulfilled, the 
Company Petition bearing C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in 
C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 is made absolute in terms of the prayer 
clauses of the said Company Scheme Petition. It shall be binding 
on the Petitioner Companies and all concerned, including their 
respective Shareholders, Creditors, Employees, and/or any other 
stakeholders. 
20. The Transferor Company is dissolved without winding up. 
21. The Income Tax Department will be at liberty to examine the 
aspects relating to any tax payable as a result of this scheme. If it is 
found that the scheme ultimately results in tax avoidance under the 
provisions of the Income Tax Act, it shall be open to the Income 
Tax authorities to take such necessary action as may be possible 
under the Income Tax Law. 
22. Needless to say, all liabilities accruing in the transferor company 
shall be transferred to the Transferee Company; however, the 
liabilities in respect of offences committed under this Act by the 
officers in default of the transferor company prior to its merger, 
amalgamation or acquisition shall continue after such merger, 

IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL 
MUMBAI BENCH-I 
 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026 
 
Page 11  
 
amalgamation or acquisition as provided in Section 240 of the 
Companies Act, 2013. 
23. The Petitioner Companies are directed to file a copy of this Order 
and a copy of the Scheme with the concerned Registrar of 
Companies electronically, along with E-Form INC-28, within 30 
days from the date of receipt of the Order by the Petitioner 
Companies. 
24. All the employees of the Transferor Company in service on the date 
immediately preceding the date on which the Scheme takes effect, 
i.e., the effective Date, shall become the employees of the 
Transferee Company on such date, without any break or 
interruption in service, and upon terms and conditions not less 
favourable than those subsisting in the concerned Transferor 
Companies on the said date. 
25. The Petitioner Companies shall lodge a copy of this order and the 
Scheme, duly authenticated by the Deputy Registrar/Assistant 
Registrar of this Tribunal, with the concerned Superintendent of 
Stamps for the purpose of adjudication of stamp duty, if any, 
payable on the same within 60 days from the date of receipt of the 
copy of the order. 
26. The present Company Scheme Petition, i.e. 
C.P.(CAA)/141/MB/2026 in C.A.(CAA)/96/MB/2026, is allowed 
and disposed of, ordered accordingly. 
 
 
 Sd/- Sd/- 
Sh. Prabhat Kumar               Sh. Sushil Mahadeorao Kochey

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
1. Further to our earlier intimations, including that dated February 2, 2025, and pursuant to 
Regulation 30 read with Para A(20) of Part A of Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”) and the SEBI Master 
Circular dated January 30, 2026, we inform you that the Company received by e- mail, on 
November 20, 2026, two Orders -in-Appeal dated November 19, 2026 passed by the 
Commissioner (Appeals), Central Goods and Services Tax, Chandigarh, rel ating to the 
Company’s Chandigarh registration. Each Order disposes of cross -appeals filed by the 
Company and the Department: 
 
a) Order-in-Appeal No. CHD -CGST-001-APPL-COMM-127-128/2026-27 (“Order 127–
128”), for July 2017 to March 2020, against Order -in-Original No. 
98/GST/ADC/CHD/2024-25 dated January 31, 2025; and 
b) Order-in-Appeal No. CHD -CGST-001-APPL-COMM-129-130/2026-27 (“Order 129–
130”), for April 2020 to March 2021, against Order -in-Original No. 
111/GST/ADC/CHD/2024-25 dated February 25, 2025. 
 
2. The outcome of each Order is as follows:  
a) Order 127–128: the Department’s appeal on demands dropped in the Order -in-Original 
has been allowed, and those demands have been confirmed. The Company’s appeal has 
been rejected, save on one issue, on which a demand of ₹1.02 crore has been set aside 
in th e Company’s favour. Tax demand confirmed: ₹87.94 crore, besides standalone 
interest demands of ₹0.22 crore 
b) Order 129–130: the Department’s appeal on demands dropped in the Order -in-Original 
has been allowed, and those demands have been confirmed. The Company’s appeal has 
been rejected, save on one issue, on which a demand of ₹0.19 crore has been set aside 
in the Company’s favour. Tax demand confirmed: ₹29.64 crore. 
 
The aggregate tax demand confirmed under the two Orders is ₹117.58 crore, together with 
consequential interest under Section 50 of the CGST Act, 2017, as applicable (not quantified in the 
Orders), and penalty as directed therein. 
 
3. Of the tax demand confirmed, ₹112.22 crore (about 95%) – ₹83.23 crore under Order 127–128 
and ₹28.99 crore under Order 129–130 – arises from a single issue: GST sought at the 
Company’s Chandigarh registration at the stage of receipt of advances from customers, against 
advance receipts issued at the Company’s stores across India (treated in the Orders as 

 
 
 
“vouchers”). Applicable GST on the goods supplied against these advances has already been 
discharged by the respective GST registrations of the Company at the time of supply of goods 
and issuance of tax invoices. Consequently, the demand would subject the same value to 
tax twice. In both Orders -in-Original, the adjudicating authority had dropped this demand in 
respect of the Company’s registrations outside Chandigarh; the Commissioner (Appeals) has 
taken a different view on the Department’s appeals.  
 
4. Based on the facts and the applicable law, the Company has a strong case on merits in respect 
of both Orders and will pursue appropriate legal remedies before the competent judicial / 
appellate forums. Penalty and interest are consequential to the tax demand and will be 
contested with it. The orders do not have any material impact on the financial, operational, 
or other activities of the Company. 
 
5. The information as required to be disclosed under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations 
read with  Master Circular dated January 30, 2026 issued by SEBI is enclosed herewith as 
Annexure A. 
 
6. The disclosure as required under Regulation 30(13) of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with 
Circular dated February 25, 2025, on Industry Standards Note on Regulation 30 of the SEBI 
Listing is enclosed herewith in Form A, as Annexure B. 
 
7. We hereby state and confirm that the information and details provided in Annexure B, in 
compliance with the Regulation 30(13) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, is true, correct and complete to the best of our knowledge 
and belief. 
 
Further updates will be provided in accordance with the Listing Regulations. Kindly take the above on 
record. 
 
For Ethos Limited 
 
 
 
 
Priya Grover

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
1. Further to our earlier intimations, including that dated February 2, 2025, and pursuant to 
Regulation 30 read with Para A(20) of Part A of Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”) and the SEBI Master 
Circular dated January 30, 2026, we inform you that the Company received by e- mail, on 
November 20, 2026, two Orders -in-Appeal dated November 19, 2026 passed by the 
Commissioner (Appeals), Central Goods and Services Tax, Chandigarh, rel ating to the 
Company’s Chandigarh registration. Each Order disposes of cross -appeals filed by the 
Company and the Department: 
 
a) Order-in-Appeal No. CHD -CGST-001-APPL-COMM-127-128/2026-27 (“Order 127–
128”), for July 2017 to March 2020, against Order -in-Original No. 
98/GST/ADC/CHD/2024-25 dated January 31, 2025; and 
b) Order-in-Appeal No. CHD -CGST-001-APPL-COMM-129-130/2026-27 (“Order 129–
130”), for April 2020 to March 2021, against Order -in-Original No. 
111/GST/ADC/CHD/2024-25 dated February 25, 2025. 
 
2. The outcome of each Order is as follows:  
a) Order 127–128: the Department’s appeal on demands dropped in the Order -in-Original 
has been allowed, and those demands have been confirmed. The Company’s appeal has 
been rejected, save on one issue, on which a demand of ₹1.02 crore has been set aside 
in th e Company’s favour. Tax demand confirmed: ₹87.94 crore, besides standalone 
interest demands of ₹0.22 crore 
b) Order 129–130: the Department’s appeal on demands dropped in the Order -in-Original 
has been allowed, and those demands have been confirmed. The Company’s appeal has 
been rejected, save on one issue, on which a demand of ₹0.19 crore has been set aside 
in the Company’s favour. Tax demand confirmed: ₹29.64 crore. 
 
The aggregate tax demand confirmed under the two Orders is ₹117.58 crore, together with 
consequential interest under Section 50 of the CGST Act, 2017, as applicable (not quantified in the 
Orders), and penalty as directed therein. 
 
3. Of the tax demand confirmed, ₹112.22 crore (about 95%) – ₹83.23 crore under Order 127–128 
and ₹28.99 crore under Order 129–130 – arises from a single issue: GST sought at the 
Company’s Chandigarh registration at the stage of receipt of advances from customers, against 
advance receipts issued at the Company’s stores across India (treated in the Orders as 

 
 
 
“vouchers”). Applicable GST on the goods supplied against these advances has already been 
discharged by the respective GST registrations of the Company at the time of supply of goods 
and issuance of tax invoices. Consequently, the demand would subject the same value to 
tax twice. In both Orders -in-Original, the adjudicating authority had dropped this demand in 
respect of the Company’s registrations outside Chandigarh; the Commissioner (Appeals) has 
taken a different view on the Department’s appeals.  
 
4. Based on the facts and the applicable law, the Company has a strong case on merits in respect 
of both Orders and will pursue appropriate legal remedies before the competent judicial / 
appellate forums. Penalty and interest are consequential to the tax demand and will be 
contested with it. The orders do not have any material impact on the financial, operational, 
or other activities of the Company. 
 
5. The information as required to be disclosed under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations 
read with  Master Circular dated January 30, 2026 issued by SEBI is enclosed herewith as 
Annexure A.

Circular dated February 25, 2025, on Industry Standards Note on Regulation 30 of the SEBI 
Listing is enclosed herewith in Form A, as Annexure B. 
 
7. We hereby state and confirm that the information and details provided in Annexure B, in 
compliance with the Regulation 30(13) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, is true, correct and complete to the best of our knowledge 
and belief. 
 
Further updates will be provided in accordance with the Listing Regulations. Kindly take the above on 
record. 
 
For Ethos Limited 
 
 
 
 
Priya Grover

Dear Sir/ Madam, 
 
Sub: Disclosure under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”) – Intimation of order passed 
 
Ref:  Stock Exchange intimation filed vide reference no. 01/2026-27 dated April 01, 2026 
With reference to the captioned subject, and in earlier intimations as referred above, the Company had 
informed the stock exchanges about receipt of order from the office of the commissioner of Income tax 
(Appeals), National Faceless Appeals Centre, Delhi, for the period AY 2020-21. 
 
Accordingly, company had filed an appeal against the said order before The Income tax Appellate Tribunal, 
Mumbai. In this regard, the company has now received a favourable order from the office of The Income 
Tax Appellate Tribunal Mumbai by directing the AO to fresh examination of the additional evidence 
submitted by Assessee, verify the supporting books, afford the assessee reasonable opportunity of hearing 
and pass a speaking order in accordance with law in case of disallowance of provision for warranty and 
after sales services.

of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, (“SEBI LODR”) and with

Dear Sir / Madam,  
 
 
 
Sub: Disclosure under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015. 
 
This is to inform you that Aarti Surfactants Limited (“Company”) has received an Order dated November 
20, 2026, from the Commissioner of Customs (NS-I), JNCH, Nhava Sheva, the details of which are set out 
below. 
 
The said Order is addressed to Aarti Industries Limited (Surfactant Specialties Division) and Mr. Nikhil 
Desai, Executive Director, and pertains to the Show Cause Notice dated March 14, 2017, issued by the 
Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Ahmedab ad, prior to the demerger and incorporation of the 
Company. 
 
In this regard, we wish to clarify that the alleged contraventions relate to the erstwhile Surfactant 
Specialties Division of Aarti Industries Limited and pertain to the period prior to the demerger. Pursuant 
to the demerger of the said division from Aarti  Industries Limited, the proceedings arising out of the 
aforesaid Show Cause Notice were transferred to the Company, being the Resultant Company under the 
Composite Scheme of Arrangement. 
 
The requisite details pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and Regulation 30(13) read with the Industry Standards on 
Regulation 30, are enclosed herewith as Annexure A. 
 
Further, we hereby state and declare that the information and details provided in Annexure A , in 
compliance with Regulation 30(13) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, are true, correct and complete to the best of our knowledge and belief. 
 
The above information is also available on the website of the Company at www.aarti-surfactants.com 

 
 
 
 
Kindly take the above information on record. 
 
Thanking you,  
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Aarti Surfactants Limited 
 
 
 
Priyanka Chaurasia 
Company Secretary 
ICSI M. NO. A44258

/ Nature and details of the order

communication 
The Adjudicating Authority, vide its Order dated

dropping the demand of Rs. 5,43,31,643/ - in respect of  
goods imported under Advance Authorization. The 
Order further directs the confiscation of imported goods 
having an aggregate value of Rs. 5,22,20,186/ -, with an 
option for redemption upon payment of the prescribed 
fine; appropriates Customs Duty amounting  to Rs. 
1,15,44,427/- already paid by the Company, against the

imposes a penalty equivalent to the duty amount and 
applicable interest; directs enforcement of the Bond and

and imposes a penalty of Rs. 1,50,000/ - on Mr. Nikhil 
Desai. 
6. Period for which the

2026-2027

contravention(s) / aberrations or 
non-compliances identified by the 
authority 
The Order alleges that the Company imported goods

them under an incorrect Customs Tariff Item (CTI), and 
that the goods were therefore not eligible for the 
exemption.

restriction or sanction imposed 
pursuant to the communication / 
order 
Please refer to Point No.5 above

The Company is assessing the overall financial impact of

The Company is examining the said Order and shall take

The Company will continue to monitor the matter and any

shall be reported in accordance with Regulation 30 of the 
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, including through the quarterly 
Integrated Fil ing (Governance) under the head 
“Disclosure of Updates to Ongoing Tax Litigations or 
Disputes”, as applicable. 
11. Any other relevant information The alleged contraventions relate to the erstwhile 
Surfactant Specialties Division of Aarti Industries Limited 
and pertain to the period prior to the demerger. Pursuant 
to the demerger of the said division from Aarti Industries 
Limited, the proceedings aris ing out of the aforesaid 
Show Cause Notice were transferred to the Company, 
being the Resultant Company under the Composite 
Scheme of Arrangement.

INTERARCH BUILDING SOLUTIONS LIMITED 
(Formerly known as Interarch Building Products Limited) 
Head Office : B-30, Sector 57, Noida - 201301, India. 
Tel.: +91 120 4170200, CIN: L45201DL1983PLC017029 
Registered Office: Farm No-8, Khasra No. 56/23/2, Dera Mandi Road, Mandi Village, Tehsil Mehrauli, New Delhi - 110047, India. 
 
Date: 21ST November, 2026 
 
  
Sub: Disclosure under Regulation 30 read with Para A(19) and Para B(8) of Part A of Schedule III 
and Regulation 30(13) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015 – Receipt of Show Cause Notice in connection with block assessment proceedings under the 
Income-tax Act, 1961 for the block period from April 1, 2019 to October 17, 2025 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
This is with reference to our earlier intimations dated August 18, 2025, August 22, 2025, January 29, 
2026 and September 15, 2026, regarding the search action initiated under Section 132 of the 
Income-tax Act, 1961 by the Income Tax Department. 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Para A(19) and Para B(8) of Part A of Schedule III and Regulation 
30(13) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("Listing 
Regulations"), and in continuation of our earlier intimations referred to above, we wish to inform 
you that the Company has received a Show Cause Notice on November 21, 2026, at 2:30 P.M. (IST), 
from the Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-7, Delhi, in connection 
with the block assessment proceedings for the period April 1, 2019 to October 17, 2025, pursuant to 
the search and seizure action conducted under Section 132 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

source_data.attchmntText: Om Freight Forwarders Limited has informed the Exchange about Action(s) taken or orders passed
source_data.voiceSummary: OM Freight Forwarders Limited intimates that search proceedings by the Maharashtra GST Department at its Corporate Office, initiated on 18th November 2026, concluded on 24th November 2026 at 11:35 P.M. The Department quantified an aggregate amount of approximately Rs. 4.99 crore, including interest. This comprises Rs. 2.51 crore for GST payable under the Reverse Charge Mechanism on import of services and legal services, Rs. 1.60 crore for reversal of Input Tax Credit relating to IPO expenses, and Rs. 0.88 crore for interest and other adjustments. The Company states it will discharge the Rs. 2.51 crore RCM liability and is eligible for corresponding Input Tax Credit. It disagrees with the proposed Rs. 1.60 crore reversal of Input Tax Credit and has submitted written objections. The net financial cost is approximately Rs. 0.88 crore. The Company reports no material impact on financials or operations beyond these amounts.

source_data.voiceSummary: Atlanta Electricals Limited received a Letter of Intent from Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh Limited for an order worth Rs 523.21 crore net of GST. The contract involves the design, manufacture, testing, and supply of 95 units of 50 MVA, 132/33 KV Power Transformers under Tender Specification No. PMM23-e68-2026. The order is split into two lots. Lot 1 comprises 50 units, with four transformers to be supplied within eight months from the Letter of Intent date, followed by four units per month. Lot 2 comprises 45 units, with four transformers to be supplied within eight months from the Letter of Intent date, followed by four units per month. The entity awarding the order is a domestic entity. There is no interest held by promoters or group companies in the awarding entity, and the transaction does not fall within related party transactions.

APTRANSCO contract for 4,750 MVA transformer capacity 
Company wins order for supply of 95 units of 50 MVA, 132/33 kV Power Transformers 
Anand (Gujarat), November 25, 2026: Atlanta Electricals Limited (NSE, BSE: ATLANTAELE), a 
leading manufacturer of power transformers, has secured an order worth approximately Rs 523.21 
crore from Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh Limited (APTRANSCO) for the design, 
manufacture, testing and supply of power transformers. 
 
As per the Letter of Intent received from APTRANSCO, the order comprises the supply of 95 units of 
50 MVA, 132/33 kV Power Transformers, aggregating 4,750 MVA of transformation capacity, 
including 50 units under Lot-1 and 45 units under Lot-2, with an aggregate contract value of 
approximately Rs 523.21 crore, net of GST. 
 
This order builds on Atlanta Electricals' existing engagement with APTRANSCO, following the 
Company's earlier order for the supply of transformers aggregating 3,120 MVA, valued at 
approximately Rs 270 crore, further strengthening its relationship with one of India's leading state 
transmission utilities. 
 
"India's power sector continues to witness sustained investments in transmission infrastructure, 
driven by rising electricity demand.  Utilities across the country are strengthening their 
transmission networks to ensure reliable and efficient power evacuation, creating significant 
opportunities for technologically advanced transformer solutions. This order from APTRANSCO 
reflects our longstanding partnership and reinforces Atlanta Electricals' commitment to supporting 
the development of resilient and future-ready transmission networks. We remain focused on 
delivering high-quality products and execution excellence as utilities undertake capacity expansion 
and network strengthening projects across the country," said Mr. Niral Patel, Chairman and 
Managing Director, Atlanta Electricals Limited. 
 
The order has been awarded under Tender Specification No. PMM23-E-68/2026 and covers the 
design, manufacture, testing and supply of the transformers on a free-at-destination basis, 
including unloading, in accordance with the technical specifications and commercial terms 
stipulated by APTRANSCO. Deliveries are scheduled to commence within eight months from the 
date of the Letter of Intent, with subsequent supplies to be executed in a phased manner. 
 
This order further strengthens Atlanta Electricals' presence in the domestic power transmission 
segment and reinforces its capability to execute large-scale transformer projects for leading 
transmission utilities. The addition of this order provides strong revenue visibility and reflecting the 
growing demand for transmission infrastructure investments across India.

from 5 MVA/11 kV up to 500 MVA/765 kV, as well as auto transformers, inverter duty transformers, 
furnace transformers, generator transformers and special duty transformers in India, across its 
manufacturing facilities in Gujarat and Karnataka.

PRESS RELEASE 
Diamond Power bags further conductor orders of Rs. 488 crore for a ±800 kV Bhadla–
Fatehpur HVDC line 
Two orders from Adani Energy Solutions for over 6,600 km of AL-59 conductors for one of India’s largest 
green energy corridors 
• Aggregate purchase order value Rs. 488.18 crore including GST (Rs. 413.71 crore excluding GST) 
• 6,660 km of AL-59 Lapwing and AL-59 Zebra conductors for the Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh 
portions of an ±800 kV HVDC transmission line 
• Further strengthens Diamond Power’s position in the HVDC transmission business 
Ahmedabad, 25 November 2026: Diamond Power Infrastructure Limited (“Diamond Power” / “DICABS”) 
(BSE: 522163 | NSE: DIACABS), India’s fastest growing cables and conductors company, today announced 
that it has received two purchase orders from Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL) for supply of AL-59 
conductors for the Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh portions of the ±800 kV HVDC Bhadla–Fatehpur 
transmission project. 
The orders together cover 5,693 km of AL-59 Lapwing conductor and 967 km of AL-59 Zebra conductor, 
aggregating 6,660 km, on delivered-at-site basis. The aggregate purchase order value is Rs. 488.18 crore 
including GST (basic value Rs. 413.71 crore excluding GST). Deliveries will be made month-wise in line 
with the project schedule and are to be completed by 31 December 2027. 
Growing presence in HVDC 
These orders follow Diamond Power’s earlier order of Rs. 707.80 crore for the same project, taking the 
Company’s total orders for the Bhadla–Fatehpur HVDC line to about Rs. 1,196 crore including GST, and 
further strengthen its position in the HVDC business. HVDC is the technology used to move very large 
blocks of power over long distances with low losses, and ±800 kV is the highest HVDC voltage level in 
operation in India. Conductors for such lines are large-diameter, high-capacity products made to 
demanding quality and surface-finish requirements, and are supplied by a limited set of qualified 
manufacturers. 
About the project 
The Bhadla–Fatehpur HVDC link is being developed by Adani Energy Solutions as a ±800 kV, 6,000 MW 
corridor of about 950 km connecting Bhadla in Rajasthan with Fatehpur in Uttar Pradesh, to evacuate 
renewable energy from Rajasthan to demand centres in northern India. 

           DIAMOND POWER INFRASTRUCTURE LIMITED 
 
   Regd. Office: Westgate (True Value) D Wing,

Makarba, Ahmedabad, Gujarat – 380051

Management comment 
Mr. Kavish Shah, Vice President – Corporate Strategy, Diamond Power Infrastructure Limited, said: 
These repeat orders for the Bhadla–Fatehpur HVDC line reflect the continued confidence Adani Energy 
Solutions has placed in Diamond Power. Conductors for a ±800 kV HVDC line must meet some of the most 
demanding specifications in the industry, and being entrusted with them strengthens our position in this 
specialised segment. With integrated aluminium rod mills, expanded conductor capacity and in-house 
testing facilities, we are well placed to execute on schedule and to participate in the HVDC and green 
energy corridor projects being planned across the country" 
Diamond Power’s conductor capability 
Diamond Power is amongst the largest conductor manufacturers in India, with integrated aluminium rod 
mills and a conductor range covering ACSR, AL-59, AAAC and HTLS conductors. The Company’s plant at 
Vadodara is supported by NABL-accredited in-house laboratories with high-voltage test facilities rated up 
to 765 kV. 
About Diamond Power Infrastructure Ltd 
Diamond Power Infrastructure Limited (DICABS) is an integrated manufacturer of power transmission 
equipment, offering LV, MV, HV and EHV power cables, control and instrumentation cables, fire-resistant 
and flame-retardant cables, solar DC and EV charging cables, and conductors, serving sectors including 
power, infrastructure, oil & gas, renewables, real estate and data centers.

PRESS RELEASE
PTC Industries Secures Major Indian Defence
Order for 400 Tonnes of Titanium Products,
Strengthening India's Defence Self-Reliance
Lucknow, India – 23 November 2026 – PTC Industries Limited, a leading Indian manufacturer of advanced materials and
high-performance engineering components, has secured a contract from the Indian Defence Sector for the supply of
approximately 400 tonnes of Titanium ingots, bars and rods.
The contract represents a significant addition to the Company’s defence order book and reinforces its position as a
domestic supplier of strategically important Titanium products for critical defence applications. The materials supplied
under the contract are intended to support defence systems requiring high strength, corrosion resistance, dimensional
stability and long-term operational reliability under demanding service conditions.
Titanium is recognised as a strategic engineering material across the defence, aerospace, marine and nuclear sectors
owing to its exceptional mechanical properties, low density and superior resistance to corrosion. Establishing indigenous
manufacturing capabilities for such critical materials is fundamental to strengthening India’s strategic supply-chain
resilience and reducing dependence on imports for advanced defence applications.
The order is aligned with the Government of India’s ongoing efforts to promote indigenous manufacturing under the
Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and supports the broader objective of increasing domestic value addition in defence
production. By expanding the indigenous availability of high-performance Titanium products, the contract contributes to
the development of a robust domestic ecosystem for strategic materials and advanced manufacturing technologies.
PTC Industries, through its wholly owned subsidiary Aerolloy Technologies Limited, has made significant investments in
developing advanced Titanium and Superalloy manufacturing capabilities in India. These investments encompass
specialised alloy melting and ingot production, forging, the development of mill products, precision casting, inspection
and testing, supported by advanced metallurgical expertise and quality assurance systems. By progressively integrating
critical stages of the manufacturing value chain, the Group is building greater control over material quality, traceability,
manufacturing processes and supply reliability. These capabilities are aimed at meeting the stringent requirements of
defence and aerospace applications and strengthening India’s indigenous advanced materials manufacturing base.
Beyond its commercial significance, the contract is expected to contribute to India’s advanced manufacturing ecosystem
by supporting technology development, expanding specialised industrial capabilities, creating opportunities for skilled
employment and strengthening domestic supply chains for critical materials. Such initiatives are integral to achieving
greater self-reliance in strategic manufacturing while enhancing the global competitiveness of India’s defence industry.
The contract also reflects the increasing participation of Indian industry in developing an indigenous defence
manufacturing base and underscores the importance of sustained collaboration between the armed forces and
domestic manufacturers in advancing national capabilities across strategically important sectors.

Chairman and Managing Director’s Statement
Mr. Sachin Agarwal, Chairman & Managing Director, PTC Industries Limited, said:
“We are grateful for the confidence placed in PTC Industries through this order. Supplying approximately 400 tonnes
of Titanium ingots, bars and rods for India’s defence requirements is a strong validation of the integrated materials
capability that we have been building over several years – from alloy melting and ingot production to forging and
mill products.
Titanium sits at the very foundation of modern defence and aerospace systems, and the ability to produce it reliably at
scale is a measure of strategic independence. This order demonstrates that PTC ONE™ – From Melt to Mission™ is
now delivering at meaningful volumes, and that critical materials India has long sourced from abroad can be produced
here, to the most exacting standards. We will continue to invest with patience and purpose in capabilities that help
India stand at par with the world.”
Advanced Manufacturing & Technology Centre (AMTC), Lucknow
ABOUT PTC INDUSTRIES LIMITED
PTC Industries Limited is an Indian advanced manufacturing company specialising in critical materials, high-integrity
precision castings and complex engineering components for aerospace, defence, space, energy and other technology-
intensive industries.
Through its wholly owned subsidiary, Aerolloy Technologies Limited, the Group is developing an integrated manufacturing
platform for Titanium and Superalloy materials, including advanced alloy melting, ingot production, forging, rolling and mill
products, alongside precision investment castings, special processes and high-precision machining capabilities.
Guided by its PTC ONE™ — From Melt to Mission™ strategy, the Group is focused on bringing together advanced materials,
metallurgy and manufacturing technologies within an integrated industrial system. Its long-term objective is to establish
globally competitive capabilities in critical materials and mission-critical components, supporting India’s strategic self-reliance
while serving the requirements of international aerospace, defence, space and energy industries.
PTC ONE™ - from Melt to Mission™ Compounding Capability. Creating Value.

PRESS RELEASE
PTC Industries Secures Major Indian Defence
Order for 400 Tonnes of Titanium Products,
Strengthening India's Defence Self-Reliance
Lucknow, India – 23 November 2026 – PTC Industries Limited, a leading Indian manufacturer of advanced materials and
high-performance engineering components, has secured a contract from the Indian Defence Sector for the supply of
approximately 400 tonnes of Titanium ingots, bars and rods.
The contract represents a significant addition to the Company’s defence order book and reinforces its position as a
domestic supplier of strategically important Titanium products for critical defence applications. The materials supplied
under the contract are intended to support defence systems requiring high strength, corrosion resistance, dimensional
stability and long-term operational reliability under demanding service conditions.
Titanium is recognised as a strategic engineering material across the defence, aerospace, marine and nuclear sectors
owing to its exceptional mechanical properties, low density and superior resistance to corrosion. Establishing indigenous
manufacturing capabilities for such critical materials is fundamental to strengthening India’s strategic supply-chain
resilience and reducing dependence on imports for advanced defence applications.
The order is aligned with the Government of India’s ongoing efforts to promote indigenous manufacturing under the
Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and supports the broader objective of increasing domestic value addition in defence
production. By expanding the indigenous availability of high-performance Titanium products, the contract contributes to
the development of a robust domestic ecosystem for strategic materials and advanced manufacturing technologies.
PTC Industries, through its wholly owned subsidiary Aerolloy Technologies Limited, has made significant investments in
developing advanced Titanium and Superalloy manufacturing capabilities in India. These investments encompass
specialised alloy melting and ingot production, forging, the development of mill products, precision casting, inspection
and testing, supported by advanced metallurgical expertise and quality assurance systems. By progressively integrating
critical stages of the manufacturing value chain, the Group is building greater control over material quality, traceability,
manufacturing processes and supply reliability. These capabilities are aimed at meeting the stringent requirements of
defence and aerospace applications and strengthening India’s indigenous advanced materials manufacturing base.
Beyond its commercial significance, the contract is expected to contribute to India’s advanced manufacturing ecosystem
by supporting technology development, expanding specialised industrial capabilities, creating opportunities for skilled
employment and strengthening domestic supply chains for critical materials. Such initiatives are integral to achieving
greater self-reliance in strategic manufacturing while enhancing the global competitiveness of India’s defence industry.
The contract also reflects the increasing participation of Indian industry in developing an indigenous defence
manufacturing base and underscores the importance of sustained collaboration between the armed forces and
domestic manufacturers in advancing national capabilities across strategically important sectors.
PTC INDUSTRIES LIMITED · CIN L27109UP1963PLC002931
Tel: +91 522 7111017 · Fax: +91 522 2265302 · Email: info@ptcil.com · www.ptcil.com Page 1 of 2

Chairman and Managing Director’s Statement
Mr. Sachin Agarwal, Chairman & Managing Director, PTC Industries Limited, said:
“We are grateful for the confidence placed in PTC Industries through this order. Supplying approximately 400 tonnes
of Titanium ingots, bars and rods for India’s defence requirements is a strong validation of the integrated materials
capability that we have been building over several years – from alloy melting and ingot production to forging and
mill products.
Titanium sits at the very foundation of modern defence and aerospace systems, and the ability to produce it reliably at
scale is a measure of strategic independence. This order demonstrates that PTC ONE™ – From Melt to Mission™ is
now delivering at meaningful volumes, and that critical materials India has long sourced from abroad can be produced
here, to the most exacting standards. We will continue to invest with patience and purpose in capabilities that help
India stand at par with the world.”
Advanced Manufacturing & Technology Centre (AMTC), Lucknow
ABOUT PTC INDUSTRIES LIMITED
PTC Industries Limited is an Indian advanced manufacturing company specialising in critical materials, high-integrity
precision castings and complex engineering components for aerospace, defence, space, energy and other technology-
intensive industries.
Through its wholly owned subsidiary, Aerolloy Technologies Limited, the Group is developing an integrated manufacturing
platform for Titanium and Superalloy materials, including advanced alloy melting, ingot production, forging, rolling and mill
products, alongside precision investment castings, special processes and high-precision machining capabilities.
Guided by its PTC ONE™ — From Melt to Mission™ strategy, the Group is focused on bringing together advanced materials,
metallurgy and manufacturing technologies within an integrated industrial system. Its long-term objective is to establish
globally competitive capabilities in critical materials and mission-critical components, supporting India’s strategic self-reliance
while serving the requirements of international aerospace, defence, space and energy industries.
PTC ONE™ - from Melt to Mission™ Compounding Capability. Creating Value.

Titagarh Rail Systems bags new order from JSW for 181 BFNSM1 wagons and 3 BVCM wagons. 
Gets approval to manufacture auto carrier wagons expanding its product offering 
 
Kolkata, 23 November, 2026: Titagarh Rail Systems Limited has further strengthened its position in the freight 
wagon industry by bagging an order from JSW(South) Rail Logistics Pvt Ltd. for INR. 77.09 crs.  
In addition, it received route clearance from Indian railways to manufacture and despatch specialised auto carrier 
wagons which enable Titagarh to become one of the few wagon manufacturers to have the capability of 
producing all kind of Freight wagons from pressurised tank wagons to carry gas and petroleum products to 
carrying all kind of automobiles.  
The approval from the railway authorities for the operation and movement of auto carrier wagons connects its 
Bharatpur Manufacturing Unit to the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) network.  
Automobile movement on rail has caught momentum recently and the market of auto carriers has been very 
buoyant over the last few months. In absence of this approval, Titagarh was unable to address this growing 
market segment in absence of this approval which Titagarh plans to get very actively engaged in doing based on 
the approval. Titagarh has also started taking steps to manufacture a prototype wagon for these auto carriers in 
order to offer shorter delivery timelines to the customers. 
Commenting on the development, Shri Umesh Chowdhary, Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Titagarh Rail 
Systems Limited, said: 
“The introduction of ACT wagons into our freight rolling stock portfolio marks another significant step towards 
broadening our product offerings and strengthening our capabilities in specialised freight solutions. With the 
approval for movement from our Bharatpur Manufacturing Unit to the DFCCIL network now in place, we are 
better positioned to enhance our manufacturing and delivery capabilities and contribute more meaningfully to 
the DFC network. We believe this will further strengthen the freight rail ecosystem, support greater efficiency in 
freight movement and contribute towards the national target of achieving 3,000 MT freight loading by 2027. 
This development also reinforces our commitment to the vision of Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat. We 
remain committed to supporting the Government’s vision through the development and delivery of innovative, 
reliable and indigenously manufactured rolling stock solutions that contribute to the continued growth and 
modernisation of India’s railway and freight infrastructure.” 
About Titagarh Rail Systems Limited 
Titagarh Rail Systems is a leading comprehensive mobility solution provider with a strong presence in India. With 
state-of-the-art factories in the country, we are committed to meeting the diverse requirements of passenger 
and freight rolling stock. At Titagarh, we specialize in crafting cutting-edge transportation solutions, including 
semi high-speed trains, urban metros, passenger coaches, propulsion systems, and a wide array of wagons, 
including specialized ones. With a passion for innovation and an unwavering dedication to excellence, our 
commitment lies in shaping the future of transportation, embodying the spirit of Make in India and contributing 
towards a Viksit Bharat. We strive to deliver world-class products that redefine the way people and goods move 
across the world. Explore our diverse range of products and experience the future of transportation at 
www.titagarh.in
