Mumbai; November 23, 2026: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Limited (SWREL) (BSE Scrip Code: 
542760; NSE Symbol: SWSOLAR), a leading renewable EPC has announced three marquee domestic orders 
– a 600 MWh BESS turnkey project in Gujarat awarded by a leading PSU and a solar project from a Private

being selected as an L1 bidder for a prestigious project in India. These orders mark another noteworthy 
milestone in SWREL’s growing renewable project portfolio and reinforces our position as a competitive, 
trusted reliable EPC player in India’s rapidly expanding renewable sector. We look forward to supporting our 
customer’s long-term growth, exceeding their expectations, and delivering meaningful impact as we build 
on this momentum."

engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) solutions provider. The company provides EPC services 
for utility-scale solar, floating solar, hybrid & energy storage and wind solutions and has a total portfolio of 
over 29.8 GWp (including projects commissioned and under various stages of construction). SWREL also 
manages an operation and maintenance (O&M) portfolio of 18.9 GWp solar power projects, including for

SWREL bagged three domestic orders including L1 position for a marquee 
project with a combined value of more than INR 2050 crore 
 
~ Receives 600 MWh BESS turnkey project order from a leading PSU in Gujarat 
~ Secures 350 MW Solar projects, which includes L1 position for a turnkey solar project from a 
leading PSU  
 
Mumbai; November 23, 2026: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Limited (SWREL) (BSE Scrip Code: 
542760; NSE Symbol: SWSOLAR), a leading renewable EPC has announced three marquee domestic orders 
– a 600 MWh BESS turnkey project in Gujarat awarded by a leading PSU and a solar project from a Private 
IPP in Rajasthan. The company has also recently emerged L1 for a prestigious solar turnkey project in 
Madhya Pradesh. The total value of all the projects is more than INR 2050 crore.  
 
Speaking on the new developments, Mr. Chandra Kishore Thakur, Global CEO, Sterling and Wilson 
Renewable Energy said, “We are honored and privileged to have received two significant orders and for 
being selected as an L1 bidder for a prestigious project in India. These orders mark another noteworthy 
milestone in SWREL’s growing renewable project portfolio and reinforces our position as a competitive, 
trusted reliable EPC player in India’s rapidly expanding renewable sector. We look forward to supporting our 
customer’s long-term growth, exceeding their expectations, and delivering meaningful impact as we build 
on this momentum." 
 
About Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Limited 
Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Limited (SWREL) is a global pure-play, end-to-end renewable 
engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) solutions provider. The company provides EPC services 
for utility-scale solar, floating solar, hybrid & energy storage and wind solutions and has a total portfolio of 
over 29.8 GWp (including projects commissioned and under various stages of construction). SWREL also 
manages an operation and maintenance (O&M) portfolio of 18.9 GWp solar power projects, including for 
projects constructed by third parties. Present in 28 countries today, Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy 
Limited has operations in India, South-east Asia, Middle East, Africa, Europe, Australia, and the Americas. 
Visit us – www.sterlingandwilsonre.com   
LinkedIn – https://www.linkedin.com/company/sterling-and-wilson-renewable-energy/

Larsen & Toubro Secures (Large*) Order 
for Deploying AI Cluster  
 
LTN Compute to deploy additional NVIDIA B300 GPUs at its Chennai campus to power an 
inference infrastructure provider’s AI-native platform as part of the 10,000 GPU cluster 
Mumbai, November 23, 2026: The L&T Group company, Vyoma.AI, through its AI 
infrastructure subsidiary LTN Compute, has secured a multi-year engagement with an 
inference infrastructure provider for the deployment of an additional NVIDIA B300 GPUs at 
its Chennai Data Center. 
The infrastructure will power the inference infrastructure provider’s AI-native platform, 
enabling it to train, fine-tune and deploy specialised AI models for high-performance 
inference at commercial scale. This development strengthens India’s AI infrastructure while 
supporting growing global demand for advanced compute. 
The integrated AI Factory will bring together hyperscale data center infrastructure, 
accelerated computing, high-performance networking, ultra-low-latency interconnects, 
high-throughput parallel storage and comprehensive AI infrastructure operations to enable 
efficient deployment of demanding AI workloads.  
The AI Factory is being developed at Vyoma.AI’s Chennai campus, envisioned as a gigawatt-
scale AI infrastructure hub. Its Phase 1 is designed for 250 MW, supported by 150 MVA power 
infrastructure readiness, providing a scalable foundation for future capacity expansion. 
“Artificial Intelligence is transforming industries, and AI Factories will provide the 
foundational infrastructure to power this transformation. This additional GPU deployment 
marks another significant milestone in L&T’s vision to build world-class AI infrastructure in 
India. Our Chennai AI Factory will deliver the scale, performance and resilience required to 
accelerate global AI innovation and strengthen India’s position as a leading hub for next-
generation computing”, said Mr S N Subrahmanyan, Chairman & Managing Director, Larsen 
& Toubro. 
LTN Compute is building next generation AI-ready digital infrastructure across India through 
hyperscale AI data centers, sovereign cloud platforms, AI Factory services, Bare Metal-as-a-
Service (BMaaS), GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) and managed AI platforms to support 
governments, enterprises, cloud providers and AI innovators.

This intimation is filed under Regulation 42 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The notice was issued on 23 November 2026.

ARKADE STRENGTHENS ITS SOUTH MUMBAI FOOTPRINT WITH LANDMARK 
REDEVELOPMENT TARGETING ~1500 Cr GDV IN TARDEO 
 
~2-acre redevelopment project with a projected Gross Development Value (GDV) of ₹1,500 
crore reinforces Arkade’s growth ambitions in one of Mumbai’s most prestigious real estate 
markets. 
Mumbai, 23rd November 2026: Arkade Developers, leading luxury listed real estate 
developers in Mumbai, has announced its strategic re-entry into the coveted South Mumbai 
(SoBo) real estate market with an ambitious redevelopment project in Tardeo, marking a 
significant milestone in the company's growth journey. Building on its existing presence in 
Mazagaon, Altamount Road and Carmichael Road, Arkade is further expanding its footprint 
across South Mumbai’s premium residential landscape. 
The redevelopment project is spread across approximately 2 acres and is expected to have a 
projected Gross Development Value (GDV) of ₹1,500 crore, as a significant addition to 
Arkade’s redevelopment portfolio. The project underscores the company’s confidence in the 
long-term potential of South Mumbai and its commitment to identifying high-value 
redevelopment opportunities in established micro-markets across the city. 
Tardeo, renowned for its central location, established social infrastructure, premium 
residential character and excellent connectivity, continues to remain one of Mumbai’s most 
sought-after residential destinations. With limited availability of developable land and 
sustained demand for quality residential spaces, the micro-market presents compelling 
opportunities for thoughtfully conceptualized redevelopment. 
Arkade’s return to South Mumbai represents more than a geographic expansion; it reflects a 
strategic step towards strengthening its presence in Mumbai’s premium real estate 
landscape. Leveraging its experience in residential development and redevelopment, the 
company aims to unlock the potential of well-established urban locations through projects 
that combine contemporary aspirations with the enduring value of prime addresses. 
Speaking on the acquisition, Mr. Amit Jain, CMD of Arkade Developers, said:  
Our re-entry into South Mumbai is an important strategic milestone for Arkade. Tardeo 
represents the very essence of Mumbai's premium residential landscape, offering a rare 
combination of location, legacy and long-term value. This project reflects our confidence in 
the redevelopment potential of established neighborhoods and our ambition to create 
meaningful value in some of Mumbai's most sought-after locations. We see this as the 
beginning of an exciting new chapter in our journey in South Mumbai." 
The Tardeo project further strengthens Arkade’s development pipeline and reflects its broader 
strategy of capitalizing on Mumbai’s evolving urban landscape, particularly through 
redevelopment-led growth. As the city increasingly looks towards revitalizing established 

 
 
 
neighborhoods, Arkade aims to play a meaningful role in shaping the next phase of Mumbai’s 
residential transformation. 
Furthermore, the company is geared up for two significant launches in Q4, Arkade Ascend, 
located in Malad(W) and Arkade Thane, Kasarvadavali,  having a combined projected GDV of 
2800 Cr. 
This acquisition not only strengthens our presence in a key growth corridor but also reinforces 
our ambition to build a future-ready portfolio of landmark developments across the Mumbai 
Metropolitan Region”. 
 
About Arkade Developers Ltd:  
Arkade Developers is a leading luxury real estate developer in Mumbai and is listed on both 
the exchanges, BSE (544261) and NSE (ARKADE). With a rich legacy spanning over 40 years, 
the company has established itself as a symbol of quality and excellence. 
Under the leadership of Chairman and Managing Director Mr. Amit Jain, Arkade Developers 
has transformed into one of Mumbai’s most respected real estate firms. The company has 
completed 33 projects under his vision and created homes for over 5,800 happy families. 
Guided by the core philosophy of "Family First," Arkade Developers focuses on building 
family-friendly homes and upholds values such as trust, transparency, commitment, and 
happiness. Known for its timely project deliveries, Arkade Developers has made a significant 
mark in the Mumbai real estate sector, having developed over 5.8 million square feet of 
property, with an additional 3+ million square feet currently under construction. 
The company's commitment to quality is reflected in its meticulous planning, innovative 
designs, and use of advanced technologies, which ensure that every project is delivered on 
time and to the highest standards. 
 
 
 
 
 
For more information, visit: https://arkade.in/ 
 
 
40+years of legacy | 33 projects completed | 5.8+ M sq. ft. developed | 3+ M sq. ft. 
under development | 5,800+ Happy Families | Listed on BSE & NSE | Pioneers in 
Timely Delivery

Subject: Intimation under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 – Receipt of Contract from Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited for Microsoft Active 
Directory Solution 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, and the applicable SEBI circulars issued thereunder, we wish to inform you that Silver 
Touch Technologies Limited ("the Company") has received a Contract (No. GEMC-511687782323631 dated 
23rd November 2026, against GeM Bid No. GEM/2025/B/6400459) from Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited 
(GUVNL) for the Design, Supply, Rollout and Maintenance of Microsoft’s Active Directory Solution with 
required software and licenses for GUVNL and its subsidiaries. 
Key particulars of the order are set out below: 
Name of the entity 
awarding the order 
Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (GUVNL), Vadodara – Energy and 
Petrochemicals Department, Government of Gujarat, for itself and its six 
subsidiary companies (GSECL, GETCO, UGVCL, MGVCL, DGVCL and PGVCL) 
Significant terms and 
conditions of the order, in 
brief 
Turnkey design, supply, implementation, enterprise rollout and maintenance 
of Microsoft Active Directory solution on GUVNL’s on-premise infrastructure, 
covering supply of perpetual Microsoft Windows Server and Client Access 
Licenses, migration of approximately 18,000 desktops across more than 850 
locations, training and handover, and five years of AMC with on-site certified 
manpower support. Contract awarded through the GeM portal on a 
milestone-based lumpsum basis, with quarterly billing. 
Whether

awarded by

entity

migration and managed support services 
Time period for execution 
of the order 
Service period:-  implementation and rollout within 12 months, followed by 
five years of AMC and on-site support from final acceptance 

   
 
Broad consideration or 
size of the order 
₹8,60,00,000 (Rupees Eight Crore Sixty Lakh only), inclusive of all duties and 
taxes 
Whether the

at arm's length 
No 
 
Strategic Significance 
The Company has a clear and growing strategic focus on the Energy and Power sector and on critical 
infrastructure management. Power generation, transmission and distribution utilities run some of the 
country’s most essential and sensitive digital environments, where secure identity, access control and 
uninterrupted availability are fundamental to reliable 24x7 power supply. 
This order spans the entire Gujarat state power value chain – generation, transmission and distribution – 
covering approximately 18,000 endpoints across more than 850 locations, including corporate offices, power 
stations and sub-stations. It will establish a centrally managed, policy-driven identity and security backbone 
aligned with the guidelines of CERT-In, NCIIPC and the Ministry of Power. 
The order strengthens the Company’s position as a trusted technology partner to power utilities and critical 
infrastructure operators, brings multi-year recurring revenue visibility through five years of AMC and on-site 
managed support, and opens opportunities for further cybersecurity, infrastructure management and digital 
transformation engagements across the energy sector. 
The above intimation will also be made available on company’s website i.e. https://www.silvertouch.com  
Kindly take the above intimation on the record.     
Thanking you, 
 
 
Yours Faithfully, 
 
 
FOR SILVER TOUCH TECHNOLOGIES LIMITED 
 
 
RAHUL ADVANI 
COMPANY SECRETARY & COMPLIANCE OFFICER

Sub: ACME Solar Holdings Limited wins 50 MW of contracted capacity in 
GUVNL’s e-reverse auction (GUVNL-FDRE-I) 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
ACME Solar Holdings Limited (ACME) has been emerged as a successful bidder in 
GUVNL's e-reverse auction for the "Selection of RE Power Developers (RPDs) for 
Procurement of 500 MW Firm and Dispatchable Power from Grid Connected 
Renewable Energy (RE) Power Projects in India under Tariff-based Competitive 
Bidding with “Greenshoe Option” of Additional 500 MW (GUVNL-FDRE-I)" 
 
Under this tender, the company has secured 50 MW of contracted capacity at a 
discovered tariff of Rs. 4.58/kWh and will supply RTC power to the state of Gujarat. 
Under this project, the site shall be developed as a co-located Solar, Wind and 
Energy Storage System (ESS). The Letter of Award (LOA) will be awarded in due 
course. 
 
You are requested to take the same on your record. 
 
Thanking you, 
 
For ACME Solar Holdings Limited 
 
 
Rajesh Sodhi 
Company Secretary and Compliance Officer 
 
 
Note : This is voluntary submission and not to be considered as an intimation 
under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements), Regulations, 2015

Ref: Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements Regulations), 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015”) 
 
Dear Sir/ Madam,  
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015 read with the SEBI Master Circular No. 
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFDPOD2/l/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026 (“SEBI Master Circular”), we 
hereby submit disclosure regarding an Order-in-Appeal dated October 16, 2026 passed by the 
Commissioner of Customs (Appeals), Mumbai Zone-III and received on dated November 20, 2026. The 
details of the aforesaid Order-in-Appeal, as required under the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015 and the 
SEBI Master Circular, are given below:  
Sr No. Particulars Details 
1 Name of the authority  Commissioner of Customs (Appeals), Mumbai Zone-III. 
The order was passed by Shri Mahesh Kumar.

action(s) taken or order(s) 
passed; 
The Company has received an Order-in-Appeal from the 
Commissioner of Customs (Appeals), Mumbai Zone-III. 
The order disposes of cross-appeals filed by the 
Company and the Department arising from the same 
Order-in-Original in relation to duty drawback matters 
concerning the Company. The appellate authority has 
partly allowed the Company’s appeal. The order upholds 
recovery of duty drawback amounting to Rs.22,91,095/- 
along with applicable interest under Section 28AA of the 
Customs Act, 1962 subject to adjustment of amounts 
already paid by the Company.  
While a demand of Rs.71,874/- pertaining to 13 shipping 
bills is set aside and the matter has been remanded to 
the original adjudicating authority for verification and 
fresh adjudication.  
The matter relating to penalty of Rs.4,00,000/- has also 
been remanded back to the adjudication authority for 
fresh determination. 

      
 
 
The Department's appeal has been allowed to the extent 
of levy of applicable interest on the duty drawback 
amount ultimately held recoverable.

Media Release 
 
Adani Energy Solutions receives LOA for 2500 MW  
renewable round-the-clock power supply to WBSEDCL 
Ahmedabad, 21st November 2026: Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. (AESL) today said its wholly 
owned subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions Ltd. (PTSL), has received a Letter of Award 
(LoA) from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. (WBSEDCL) for supply of 1,750 
MW of Renewable Energy Round-the-Clock (RE-RTC) power for a period of 25 years. The LoA 
provides a 750 MW greenshoe option, which upon exercising, would take the aggregate 
contracted capacity to 2,500 MW. 
The award follows a competitive bidding process in which PTSL emerged as the successful 
bidder after the e-reverse auction. Power Supply is scheduled to commence from 1st July 2028 
for 1750 MW capacity and from 1st Apr 2029 for 750 MW, once greenshoe option is exercised. 
“Round-the-clock renewable power will be critical to India’s energy transition, combining the 
sustainability of renewables and optimising transmission systems usage. This significant order 
win strengthens our commitment to deliver scalable energy solutions, and allows us to partner 
with WBSEDCL in supporting West Bengal’s long-term sustinable power needs. PTSL is rapidly 
emerging as a partner of choice for bulk power consumers, with the ability to structure 
bespoke and scalable solutions around their specific energy requirements." said Mr. Kandarp 
Patel, CEO, AESL. 
The order represents a significant addition to PTSL’s expanding portfolio of energy solutions. 
While it has tied-up ~4.6 GW of solar & wind, and ~3.5 GWh of BESS capacity on the sourcing 
side, it is steadily stitching the supply side by augmenting long term supply contracts with 
bulk consumers like industries, data centres, commercial entities, and Discoms. 
About Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) 
AESL, part of the Adani portfolio, is a multidimensional organization with presence in various facets of 
the energy domain, namely power transmission, distribution, smart metering, and cooling solutions. 
AESL is the country’s largest private transmission company with a cumulative transmission network of 
30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA transformation capacity. In its retail electricity distribution business, as 
on AESL serves approximately 13 million consumers in metropolitan Mumbai and the industrial hub of 
Mundra SEZ. AESL is ramping up its smart metering business and is on course to become India’s leading 
smart metering integrator. AESL, with its integrated offering through the expansion of its distribution 
network through parallel licenses and competitive and tailored retail solutions, including a significant 
share of green power, is revolutionizing the way energy is delivered to the end consumer. AESL is a 
catalyst for transforming the energy landscape in the most reliable, affordable, and sustainable way. 
For more information, please visit www.adanienergysolutions.com 
 
For media queries, please contact: Roy Paul, roy.paul@adani.com

Media Release 
 
Adani Energy Solutions receives LOA for 2500 MW  
renewable round-the-clock power supply to WBSEDCL 
Ahmedabad, 21st November 2026: Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. (AESL) today said its wholly 
owned subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions Ltd. (PTSL), has received a Letter of Award 
(LoA) from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. (WBSEDCL) for supply of 1,750 
MW of Renewable Energy Round-the-Clock (RE-RTC) power for a period of 25 years. The LoA 
provides a 750 MW greenshoe option, which upon exercising, would take the aggregate 
contracted capacity to 2,500 MW. 
The award follows a competitive bidding process in which PTSL emerged as the successful 
bidder after the e-reverse auction. Power Supply is scheduled to commence from 1st July 2028 
for 1750 MW capacity and from 1st Apr 2029 for 750 MW, once greenshoe option is exercised. 
“Round-the-clock renewable power will be critical to India’s energy transition, combining the 
sustainability of renewables and optimising transmission systems usage. This significant order 
win strengthens our commitment to deliver scalable energy solutions, and allows us to partner 
with WBSEDCL in supporting West Bengal’s long-term sustinable power needs. PTSL is rapidly 
emerging as a partner of choice for bulk power consumers, with the ability to structure 
bespoke and scalable solutions around their specific energy requirements." said Mr. Kandarp 
Patel, CEO, AESL. 
The order represents a significant addition to PTSL’s expanding portfolio of energy solutions. 
While it has tied-up ~4.6 GW of solar & wind, and ~3.5 GWh of BESS capacity on the sourcing 
side, it is steadily stitching the supply side by augmenting long term supply contracts with 
bulk consumers like industries, data centres, commercial entities, and Discoms. 
About Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) 
AESL, part of the Adani portfolio, is a multidimensional organization with presence in various facets of 
the energy domain, namely power transmission, distribution, smart metering, and cooling solutions. 
AESL is the country’s largest private transmission company with a cumulative transmission network of 
30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA transformation capacity. In its retail electricity distribution business, as 
on AESL serves approximately 13 million consumers in metropolitan Mumbai and the industrial hub of 
Mundra SEZ. AESL is ramping up its smart metering business and is on course to become India’s leading 
smart metering integrator. AESL, with its integrated offering through the expansion of its distribution 
network through parallel licenses and competitive and tailored retail solutions, including a significant 
share of green power, is revolutionizing the way energy is delivered to the end consumer. AESL is a 
catalyst for transforming the energy landscape in the most reliable, affordable, and sustainable way. 
For more information, please visit www.adanienergysolutions.com

Press Release 
 
Jupiter Wagons secures repeat order worth over INR 128 crore 
from JSW (South) Rail Logistics 
 
National, November 20th 2026: Jupiter Wagons Limited (JWL), one of India’s leading rolling stock and mobility 
solutions companies, has received a repeat order worth over INR 128 crore from JSW (South) Rail Logistics Private 
Limited, deepening its partnership with the JSW Group. 
 
The order has been received in the form of a Letter of Intent from JSW (South) Rail Logistics Private Limited, valued 
at INR 128.61 crore (incl. GST), for the manufacture and supply of 5 BFNSM1 rakes comprising 302 BFNSM1 
wagons. 
 
This is Jupiter Wagons’ second BFNSM1 order from JSW (South) Rail Logistics, following an INR 122.88 crore order 
from the same customer in June 2026. With the latest win, the Company’s cumulative order intake from the JSW 
Group in 2026 reaches approximately INR 399 crore. 
 
The latest order sustains Jupiter Wagons’ strong run with private sector customers, which runs in parallel with a robust 
Indian Railways business that includes its recent INR 1,140 crore order from the Ministry of Railways for 2,583 
wagons. This balance across private and government demand gives the Company a diversified and resilient order book. 
 
Commenting on the development, Mr Vivek Lohia, Managing Director, Jupiter Wagons Limited, said: 
“A repeat order from the same customer is among the strongest endorsements a manufacturer can earn. JSW’s 
continued patronage underlines Jupiter Wagons’ position as a manufacturing partner of choice for private freight 
operators. As they invest more heavily in their own rolling stock, we are winning a growing share of that demand, 
even as our order flow from Indian Railways remains robust. This mix keeps our order book healthy and well spread, 
and we intend to keep earning our customers’ trust through the reliability of what we build.” 
_____________________________________________________________________________ 
 
 
About Jupiter Wagons Ltd. (JWL) (BSE: 533272; NSE: JWL) 
 
Jupiter Wagons Limited (JWL) is a provider of comprehensive mobility solutions, with diverse offerings across Freight 
Wagons, Locomotives, Commercial Vehicles, ISO Marine Containers, and products such as Couplers, Draft Gears, 
Bogies, CMS Crossings, Brake Disc, Brake System, Wheels, Axles and Wheel sets. JWL has manufacturing facilities 
located in Kolkata, Jamshedpur, Indore, Jabalpur, Bangalore and Aurangabad with full backward integration to its 
foundry operations. The group has established partnerships with leading global companies such as Tatravagonka a.s. 
(Slovakia), DAKO CZ (Czech Republic), Kovis d.o.o. (Slovenia), Talleres Alegria s.a. (Spain).  
 
With a rich legacy of over four decades, the Company has leveraged its deep technological capabilities and robust 
financial position to emerge as a one-stop shop for mobility solutions and reinforce its position as one of the fastest 
growing within the industry. Catering to industries such as Railways, Automobile, Transportation, Logistics, 
Construction Equipment, Municipalities, Healthcare, Energy, Mining and Infrastructure, the Company boasts a 

 
marquee client base including the Indian Railways, American Railroads, Indian Ministry of Defence, BEML, Alstom, 
Tata Motors, GE, Volvo Eicher Motors. For more details, please visit www.jupiterwagons.com

energy corridors

• Marks Diamond Power’s entry into the HVDC transmission business 
Vadodara / Ahmedabad, [●] November 2026: Diamond Power Infrastructure Limited (“Diamond Power” 
/ “DICABS”) (BSE: 522163 | NSE: DIACABS), India’s fastest growing cables and conductors company, today 
announced that it has received a purchase order from Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL) for supply 
of AL-59 conductors for the ±800 kV HVDC Bhadla–Fatehpur transmission project. 
The order covers 8,948 km of AL-59 Lapwing conductor and 111 km of AL-59 Moose conductor, 
aggregating 9,059 km, on delivered-at-site basis. The purchase order value is Rs. 707.80 crore including 
GST (basic value Rs. 599.83 crore excluding GST). Deliveries will be made month-wise in line with the 
project schedule and are to be completed by 31 December 2027. 
Base indices and commodity back-to-back pricing 
The Purchase Order value is based on LME aluminium of USD 2,550 per MT, premium of USD 106 per MT 
and an exchange rate of USD/INR 87. The order is on commodity back-to-back basis: the final price of 
each month’s supplies will be determined under the price variation formula on the average LME 
aluminium price and USD/INR rate of the month preceding scheduled dispatch, so that movement in 
aluminium price and exchange rate is passed through. The Company therefore does not carry aluminium 
price or currency risk on this order beyond the pricing period. 
Entry into HVDC 
This is Diamond Power’s first major order for an ±800 kV HVDC transmission line and marks the 
Company’s entry into the HVDC business. HVDC is the technology used to move very large blocks of power 
over long distances with low losses, and ±800 kV is the highest HVDC voltage level in operation in India.

Adani Energy Solutions for the confidence placed in us. With our integrated rod mills, enhanced conductor 
capacity and in-house testing facilities, we are well prepared to deliver this order on schedule and to 
participate in the HVDC and green energy corridor projects planned across the country.”

3i Infotech Limited has informed the Exchange about Bagging/Receiving of orders/contracts

November 19, 2026 
 
BSE Limited                                                    National Stock Exchange of India Limited  
Sir Phiroze Jeejeebhoy Towers                        Exchange Plaza, 5th Floor,  
Dalal Street, Fort,                                             Plot No. C-1, Block G  
Mumbai – 400 001                                           Bandra Kurla Complex,  
Security Code: 532628                                    Mumbai – 400 051  
                                                                         Scrip code: 3IINFOLTD 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Sub: Intimation under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Receipt of Purchase Order 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, we hereby inform you that 3i Infotech Limited has received a purchase order 
dated November 19, 2026, from a new customer, being a banking institution in India. 
The order covers IT Facility Management Services, comprehensive onsite annual maintenance, 
software and security subscriptions, infrastructure support and ISO certification across the 
customer's data centre, disaster recovery environment, head office and branch network. 
The committed term is three years commencing on January 1, 2027. Total Purchase Order value 
is Rs. 24.48 Crore exclusive of applicable taxes.  
The requisite details as per SEBI Master Circular HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 
dated January 30, 2026, are enclosed as Annexure A.  
The above information will also be made available on the website of the Company. 
You are requested to take the same on record. 
Thanking you, 
For 3i Infotech Limited 
 
Varika Rastogi 
Company Secretary & Compliance Officer 
 
Encl: As above

MEDIA RELEASE 
DELPHI WORLD MONEY STRENGTHENS ITS INTEGRATED TRAVEL PLATFORM 
WITH THREE-YEAR MADHYA PRADESH GOVERNMENT TRAVEL EMPANELMENT 
 
Three-year empanelment of Ebix Travels by MPSTDC expands Delphi's presence in 
government and institutional travel, covering domestic and international travel, group 
mobility and MICE services 
 
New Delhi, 19 November 2026:  Delphi World Money Limited (“Delphi”), an emerging 
integrated Travel, Financial Services and Technology platform, continues to expand its Travel 
Business as Ebix Travels Private Limited (“Ebix Travels”), has been empanelled by the Madhya 
Pradesh State Tourism Development Corporation (MPSTDC), a Government of Madhya Pradesh 
undertaking, as a tour operator for domestic and international end -to-end travel services. The 
three-year engagement represents an important addition to Delphi's growing institutional travel 
portfolio and strengthens its capabilities across government travel, group mobility, international 
delegations and Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) services. 
 
Expanding Presence in Government and Institutional Travel 
 
The empanelment follows a competitive tender process initiated by MPSTDC, the implementing 
agency for the Madhya Pradesh Government's Mukhya Mantri Tirth Darshan Yojana. Ebix 
Travels successfully qualified on both the technical and financial parameters pre scribed under 
the tender and will remain valid for a period of three years. 
 
Under the engagement, Ebix Travels will manage domestic and international travel requirements 
assigned by MPSTDC, offering a comprehensive range of services including air and railway 
ticketing, hotel accommodation, airport transfers, ground transportation,  visa and passport 
assistance, foreign exchange, travel insurance and airport protocol arrangements. The scope also 
includes customised travel itineraries, coordination of connecting flights and transfers, and end-
to-end assistance for cancellations, rebookings and other travel-related requirements. 
 
Comprehensive Travel Management and Group Mobility Solutions 
 
The engagement extends beyond conventional ticketing and accommodation services to 
encompass the coordination and management of travel and logistical requirements for official 
delegations and large groups travelling across India and overseas. 
 
These arrangements include coordination of interpreters, liaison officers, meeting rooms, 
banquet facilities and temporary office arrangements at various destinations. For international 
group travel, Ebix Travels will deploy dedicated tour managers to acco mpany delegations and 
oversee travel logistics throughout the journey, ensuring coordinated execution and on -ground 
assistance. 
 
The mandate provides an opportunity for Ebix Travels to leverage its established travel 
management capabilities across multiple service categories and deliver an integrated travel 
proposition for government and institutional customers. 
 
 
 

 
 
 
DELPHI WORLD MONEY LIMITED 
Regd. Office: 8th Floor, Manek Plaza, Kalina CST Road, Kolekalyan, Santacruz (E), Mumbai, Maharashtra-400098 
Website: www.indiaforexonline.com . E. mail :corp.relations@ebixcash.com . Phone: +91-22-68649800 
CIN: L65990MH1985PLC037697 
 
Leveraging Established MICE and Destination Management Capabilities 
 
Ebix Travels will draw upon the experience and capabilities of its established travel businesses, 
including Mercury Travels and Leisure Corp, to support the requirements under the engagement. 
The businesses have capabilities spanning corporate conferences,  incentive programmes, 
destination management, group travel, event planning and associated logistics. 
 
Its MICE business has received the National Tourism Award twice and has served as a preferred 
MICE partner for more than 150 companies, reflecting its experience in managing complex travel 
programmes and large-scale corporate and institutional engagements. 
 
These capabilities complement Delphi's broader strategy of building an integrated travel 
platform by bringing together corporate travel, leisure travel, MICE, hospitality and ancillary 
travel services, enabling the Company to pursue opportunities across a wider spectrum of 
customer segments. 
 
Positioned to Participate in India's Expanding Travel Ecosystem 
 
India's travel and tourism industry continues to offer significant growth opportunities, supported 
by rising domestic mobility, increasing international travel and growing demand for organised 
travel management solutions. According to the Ministry of Touri sm, India recorded 
approximately 428.7 crore domestic tourist visits in 2025, registering growth of around 45.5% 
over the previous year, while outbound departures by Indian nationals increased by 6.3% to 
approximately 3.3 crore. 
 
The corporate travel segment also represents a significant opportunity, with Deloitte estimating 
that India's corporate travel market could reach approximately US$20.8 billion by FY2030, 
growing at around 10.1% CAGR. 
 
Against this backdrop, Delphi is focused on expanding its Travel business beyond traditional 
ticketing services towards a broader, technology -enabled and integrated travel management 
platform. The MPSTDC empanelment further broadens the Company's addressab le customer 
base and provides an additional avenue to participate in the growing government and 
institutional travel ecosystem. 
 
Building a Diversified and Scalable Travel Platform 
 
The latest development adds to Ebix Travels' existing portfolio of government and institutional 
tourism engagements. The business also operates and manages the Deccan Odyssey luxury train 
in partnership with the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC), providing 
experience in tourism operations, destination management and travel services associated with 
government-linked initiatives. 
 
As Delphi continues to consolidate and expand its Travel operations, engagements of this nature 
are expected to complement its existing corporate travel business, strengthen institutional 
relationships and create opportunities for cross-selling and wider adoption of its integrated travel 
services. 
 
The Company remains focused on building a scalable Travel platform through deeper customer 
engagement, expansion into new business segments, technology -led service delivery and the 
utilization of synergies across its travel businesses. 

 
 
 
DELPHI WORLD MONEY LIMITED 
Regd. Office: 8th Floor, Manek Plaza, Kalina CST Road, Kolekalyan, Santacruz (E), Mumbai, Maharashtra-400098 
Website: www.indiaforexonline.com . E. mail :corp.relations@ebixcash.com . Phone: +91-22-68649800 
CIN: L65990MH1985PLC037697 
 
Management Commentary 
 
Commenting on the development, Mr . Arun Kundu, Business Head MICE , Ebix Travels , 
said: " 
 
Our empanelment by the Madhya Pradesh Government through MPSTDC is an 
important milestone in expanding our institutional and government travel business. 
It provides an opportunity to bring together our capabilities across travel 
management, international g roup travel, MICE and destination services under a 
comprehensive service proposition. We intend to focus on reliable execution, 
competitive pricing and responsive customer support, backed by dedicated local 
presence in Madhya Pradesh and 24x7 assistance. W e believe our established 
experience and integrated service capabilities will enable us to effectively serve the 
diverse travel requirements under this engagement.

Pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and 
Aptech Limited’s Policy on Determination of Materiality of Events and Information for Disclosure to the Stock 
Exchanges (“Materiality Policy”), this disclosure is made to inform you that Aptech Limited has received a Work 
Order from the autonomous body under State Government. 
 
Additional information required to be disclosed, in accordance with SEBI Circular HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-
POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, issued in connection with Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR has been set

Aptech Ltd. is a pioneer in the non-formal vocational training business in the country with a significant global 
presence. Ever since its commencement in 1986 and with a current presence of over 750+ centres globally, Aptech 
Ltd. has effectively ventured into diverse sectors ranging from IT training, media & entertainment, retail & 
aviation, beauty & wellness, banking & finance, and pre-school segment amongst others. Aptech Ltd. has 
successfully trained students, professionals, universities & corporates through its two main streams of business - 
Individual Training and Institutional Business. 
 
Under Individual Training, Aptech offers career and professional training through its multi brands - Arena 
Animation, Maya Academy of Advanced Creativity (MAAC), Lakmé Academy powered by Aptech, Aptech Learning, 
Aptech Aviation Academy, and Aptech International Preschool. Institutional Business includes training and 
assessment solutions for corporates & institutions (Aptech Training Solutions, Aptech Assessment & Testing 
Solutions). With ProAlley, Aptech offers online training in graphic design, animation, VFX and game design. 
 
This is for your information and record. 
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Aptech Limited             
 
 
 
Shruti Laud 
Company Secretary

Media Release 
 
Adani Energy Solutions wins Bihar transmission project 
Editor’s Synopsis 
• Project to evacuate 2,400 MW of power from Adani Power’s upcoming Pirpainti Ultra 
Super Critical Thermal Power Plant and strengthen Bihar’s transmission network 
• Project adds 881 ckm of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity 
to AESL's transmission portfolio 
Ahmedabad, 19 November 2026: Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL), India’s leading 
private sector power transmission and distribution company, today said it has won a 
transmission project for evacuation of power from the upcoming 2400 MW power plant in 
Pirpainti, Bihar. The project, won through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) 
mechanism, will provide annual tariff of Rs ~Rs 500 cr once commissioned.  
The project, titled, “Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti”, will be implemented through 
the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd. and will be delivered 
by the last quarter of 2028. Besides evacuation of power from the Pirpainti Power Plant, the 
project will strengthen the state’s transmission network and enhance supply reliability. 
“The Pirpainti transmission scheme will create a robust evacuation system for 2,400 MW of 
generation capacity while strengthening Bihar’s transmission backbone. It will enhance grid 
reliability and resilience and help the state meet its growing power demand. We remain 
committed to building reliable and efficient transmission infrastructure that supports the 
country’s long-term energy security,” said Mr. Kandarp Patel, CEO, Adani Energy Solutions.  
Upon completion, the project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 
3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to AESL’s portfolio, taking it to 30,683 ckm and 146,585 
MVA. With this project, AESL’s transmission capex now stands at ~Rs 91,500 crore.  
The project comprises construction of four Gas Insulated Substations (GIS) at Jhanjharpur, 
Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transformation capacity. The transmission 
infrastructure will include the 400 kV DCDS Pirpainti-Jhanjharpur, Pirpainti-Begusarai and 
Begusarai-Bakhtiyarpur lines, as well as the 220 kV DCDS Jhanjharpur-Bethauli and Begusarai-
Begusarai Town lines. It will also involve LILO of existing 220 kV and 132 kV transmission lines 
at Jhanjharpur and construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur GSS. 
About Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) 
AESL, part of the Adani portfolio, is a multidimensional organization with presence in various facets of 
the energy domain, namely power transmission, distribution, smart metering, and cooling solutions. 
AESL is the country’s largest private transmission company with a cumulative transmission network of 
30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA transformation capacity. In its retail electricity distribution business, as 
on AESL serves approximately 13 million consumers in metropolitan Mumbai and the industrial hub of 
Mundra SEZ. AESL is ramping up its smart metering business and is on course to become India’s leading 
smart metering integrator. AESL, with its integrated offering through the expansion of its distribution 
network through parallel licenses and competitive and tailored retail solutions, including a significant 
share of green power, is revolutionizing the way energy is delivered to the end consumer. AESL is a 
catalyst for transforming the energy landscape in the most reliable, affordable, and sustainable way. 
For more information, please visit www.adanienergysolutions.com 
 
For media queries, please contact: Roy Paul, roy.paul@adani.com

Media Release 
 
Adani Energy Solutions wins Bihar transmission project 
Editor’s Synopsis 
• Project to evacuate 2,400 MW of power from Adani Power’s upcoming Pirpainti Ultra 
Super Critical Thermal Power Plant and strengthen Bihar’s transmission network 
• Project adds 881 ckm of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity 
to AESL's transmission portfolio 
Ahmedabad, 19 November 2026: Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL), India’s leading 
private sector power transmission and distribution company, today said it has won a 
transmission project for evacuation of power from the upcoming 2400 MW power plant in 
Pirpainti, Bihar. The project, won through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) 
mechanism, will provide annual tariff of Rs ~Rs 500 cr once commissioned.  
The project, titled, “Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti”, will be implemented through 
the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd. and will be delivered 
by the last quarter of 2028. Besides evacuation of power from the Pirpainti Power Plant, the 
project will strengthen the state’s transmission network and enhance supply reliability. 
“The Pirpainti transmission scheme will create a robust evacuation system for 2,400 MW of 
generation capacity while strengthening Bihar’s transmission backbone. It will enhance grid 
reliability and resilience and help the state meet its growing power demand. We remain 
committed to building reliable and efficient transmission infrastructure that supports the 
country’s long-term energy security,” said Mr. Kandarp Patel, CEO, Adani Energy Solutions.  
Upon completion, the project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 
3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to AESL’s portfolio, taking it to 30,683 ckm and 146,585 
MVA. With this project, AESL’s transmission capex now stands at ~Rs 91,500 crore.  
The project comprises construction of four Gas Insulated Substations (GIS) at Jhanjharpur, 
Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transformation capacity. The transmission 
infrastructure will include the 400 kV DCDS Pirpainti-Jhanjharpur, Pirpainti-Begusarai and 
Begusarai-Bakhtiyarpur lines, as well as the 220 kV DCDS Jhanjharpur-Bethauli and Begusarai-
Begusarai Town lines. It will also involve LILO of existing 220 kV and 132 kV transmission lines 
at Jhanjharpur and construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur GSS. 
About Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) 
AESL, part of the Adani portfolio, is a multidimensional organization with presence in various facets of 
the energy domain, namely power transmission, distribution, smart metering, and cooling solutions. 
AESL is the country’s largest private transmission company with a cumulative transmission network of 
30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA transformation capacity. In its retail electricity distribution business, as 
on AESL serves approximately 13 million consumers in metropolitan Mumbai and the industrial hub of 
Mundra SEZ. AESL is ramping up its smart metering business and is on course to become India’s leading 
smart metering integrator. AESL, with its integrated offering through the expansion of its distribution 
network through parallel licenses and competitive and tailored retail solutions, including a significant 
share of green power, is revolutionizing the way energy is delivered to the end consumer. AESL is a 
catalyst for transforming the energy landscape in the most reliable, affordable, and sustainable way. 
For more information, please visit www.adanienergysolutions.com

Aurionpro secures additional order of nearly ₹100 crore from global hyperscaler, 
expands AI-ready data centre engagement in Southern India 
Expanded engagement takes total value with the customer past ₹400 crore, 
reflecting confidence in Aurionpro’s data centre capabilities and bolstering its 
order book. 
Mumbai, November 19, 2026 – Aurionpro, a leading end-to-end data centre 
solutions and enterprise technology provider, is pleased to announce an additional 
order worth close to ₹100 crore from a global hyperscaler for the development of 
an AI-ready data centre in Southern India. This order represents an expansion of 
the existing engagement with the hyperscaler, announced earlier this year, further 
strengthening the Company’s relationship with the customer.  
With this latest order, the aggregate value of engagements with the hyperscaler 
has exceeded ₹400 crore, reflecting the growing scale of the relationship. The 
project is scheduled to be executed over a period of nine months. 
Bhaskar Bhattacharya, EVP & Head – Enterprise Business, Aurionpro, said: 
“We thank our customer for their continued trust and confidence in 
Aurionpro. As demand for AI-ready infrastructure accelerates, we are 
expanding our presence across the data centre value chain. 
Alongside our delivery teams, we are investing in advanced 
manufacturing as part of a backward integration strategy. This will 
enable us to gain greater control over the supply chain, improve 
operational efficiency, and scale faster to meet the 
requirements of hyperscale clients. With growing traction 
and recent order wins, we are well positioned to further 
strengthen our presence in this market and capitalise on 
the strong demand.” 
About Aurionpro Solutions:  Aurionpro Solutions Ltd. (BSE: 532668 | NSE: AURIONPRO) is 
a global enterprise technology leader pioneering intuitive-tech through deep-tech IPs 
and scalable products. With a strong presence across Banking, Payments, Mobility, 
Insurance, Transit, Data Centers, and Government Sectors, Aurionpro is setting new 
benchmarks for AI innovation and impact. Its B2E (Business-to-Ecosystem) approach 
empowers entire ecosystems – driving growth, transformation, and scale across 
interconnected value chains. Backed by 3,000+ experts and a global-first mindset, 
Aurionpro is built to lead the next. For more information, visit us at www.aurionpro.com.

Analysis and Findings 
24. We have heard the learned counsel for the Applicant and Respondent No. 
1, Respondent No. 2 and Respondent No. 15 and perused the material on 
record. 
 
25. At the outset, we observe that during the course of hearing on 27.10.2026, 
the following order was passed: 
 
1. This is the IA filed by the RP seeking liquidation of the 
Corporate Debtor. This matter had come up for our 
consideration on 01.09.2026, wherein one last and final

27. It is further noted that the Applicant has approached this Adjudicating 
Authority seeking liquidation of the Corporate Debtor under Section 33(1) 
of the Code. In this regard, it is pertinent to refer to the relevant provisions 
of Section 33 of the Code, which deal with the initiation of liquidation 
proceedings. The same are reproduced below for ready reference: 
 
Section 33 - Initiation of liquidation 
 
(1) Where the Adjudicating Authority, — 
a) before the expiry of the insolvency resolution process period 
or the maximum period permitted for completion of the 
corporate insolvency resolution process under section 12 or 
the fast track corporate insolvency resolution process under 
section 56, as the case may be, does not receive a resolution 
plan under sub-section (6) of section 30; or 
b) rejects the resolution plan under section 31 for the non-
compliance of the requirements specified therein, 
it shall— 
(i) pass an order requiring the corporate debtor to be liquidated 
in the manner as laid down in this Chapter; 
(ii) issue a public announcement stating that the corporate debtor 
is in liquidation; and 
(iii)  require such order to be sent to the authority with which the 
corporate debtor is registered." 
 
(2) Where the resolution professional, at any time during the 
corporate insolvency resolution process but before 
confirmation of resolution plan, intimates the Adjudicating 
Authority of the decision of the committee of creditors 
approved by not less than sixty-six percent of the voting share 
to liquidate or dissolve the corporate debtor, the Adjudicating 
Authority shall pass a liquidation order as referred to in- sub-
clauses (i)(ii)(iii)(iv) and (v) of clause (b) of sub-section (1). 
 
Explanation – For the purposes of this sub-section, it is hereby 
declared that the committee of creditors may take the decision 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 14 of 18 
 
to liquidate the corporate debtor, any time after its constitution 
under sub-section (1) of section 21 and before the confirmation 
of the resolution plan, including at any time before the 
preparation of the information memorandum.” 
 
28. Section 33(1) provides that where the Adjudicating Authority does not 
receive a resolution plan before the expiry of the CIRP period or the 
maximum period permitted for completion of the CIRP, it shall pass an 
order for liquidation of the Corporate Debtor. Whereas Section 33(2) of the 
Code provides that, at any stage during the CIRP, but before the approval 
of a resolution plan by the Adjudicating Authority, the CoC may, in 
exercise of its commercial wisdom, pass a resolution to liquidate the 
Corporate Debtor by a vote of not less than 66% of the voting share. Upon 
such decision being communicated by the RP to the Adjudicating 
Authority, the Adjudicating Authority is required to pass a liquidation 
order. Thus, the existence of a CoC resolution with requisite majority, and 
the filing of the application “at any time during the CIRP”, are statutory 
preconditions for initiating liquidation under Section 33(2) of the Code. 
There is no such requirement of Section 33(1) of the Code. 
 
29. Having regard to the aforesaid provisions, it is necessary to examine the 
facts of the present case. It is noted that the CIRP of the Corporate Debtor 
commenced vide order dated 02.11.2023. During the CIRP, the Resolution 
Professional issued Form G on two occasions and several resolution plans 
were received and considered by the CoC. However, despite repeated 
deliberations none of the revised resolution plans received the requisite 
approval of 66% voting share of the CoC.  
 
30. It is further noted that the proposal for liquidation of the Corporate Debtor 
was also placed before the CoC for voting in the 20th meeting held on 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 15 of 18 
 
14.08.2025 but failed to secure the requisite majority, having received only 
43.16% votes in favour. Thereafter, in the 22nd meeting of the CoC held on 
15.11.2025 and 18.11.2025, the Resolution Professional apprised the 
members that neither any resolution plan nor the proposal for liquidation 
had secured the requisite voting share and placed various options before 
the CoC, including issuance of a fresh Form G or filing an application for 
liquidation. However, the members of the CoC remained divided on the 
proposed course of action, and no decision on any of the options was taken 
by the CoC.  
 
31. In view of the above, it is evident that despite repeated efforts and sufficient 
opportunities, the CIRP of the Corporate Debtor could not culminate in 
approval of any resolution plan within the permissible period i.e. till the 
expiry of extended CIRP Period on 20.11.2025 which was the 750th day 
from the insolvency commencement date of 02.11.2023. Accordingly, the 
provisions of Section 33(1)(a) of the Code are attracted, and the Applicant 
has rightly invoked the said provision seeking liquidation of the Corporate 
Debtor. 
 
32. As regards prayer (c), seeking condonation of delay of five days in filing 
the present Application, it is noted that the delay is minor in nature and has 
arisen in the course of filing the present Application seeking liquidation of 
the Corporate Debtor. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, 
the delay in filing the Application is hereby condoned. 
 
33. Additionally, during the hearing held on 27.10.2026, Respondent No. 2, 
Central Bank of India opposed the liquidation of the Corporate Debtor in 
view of I.A No. 711 of 2026. In this regard, we note that the said objection 
has been duly been considered by this Adjudicating Authority in I.A No. 
711 of 2026, which has been dismissed by a separate order. We further note

that despite issuance of Form G on two occasions and receipt of 14 
resolution plans, none of the plans could secure the requisite majority of 
66% voting share of the CoC. Further, no resolution was passed for

the CIRP has already continued for a substantial period without yielding 
any resolution, we find no merit in the objection raised by Respondent No. 
2 so as to warrant any further continuation of the CIRP.

IA (LIQ) NO. 94 OF 2025 
1. The present Interlocutory Application has been filed on 24.11.2025 by Mr, 
Gajesh Labchand Jain, (“Applicant”) Resolution Professional of M/s 
Compuage Infocom Limited (“Corporate Debtor”), under Section 33(1) 
of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (“the Code”), seeking 
liquidation of the Corporate Debtor with the following prayers: 
a. Allow the present application under Section 33(1) of the 
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, since none of the 
resolution plans have achieved the requisite threshold of 
66% and also on the ground that the Corporate Insolvency 
Resolution Process has exceeded the statutory period in 
spite of seeking several extensions. 
b. Pass an order directing liquidation of the Corporate 
Debtor, Compuage Infocom Limited, under Section 33(1) 
of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; 
c. Condone the delay of 5 (days) day in filing the present 
application, considering the last date for completion of 
CIRP is 20 November 2025, if extension granted by the 
Hon’ble NCLT; 
d. Issue necessary directions for public announcement of 
liquidation and for taking custody of assets, books, records, 
and properties of the Corporate Debtor; 
e. Pass such other or further orders as this Hon’ble Tribunal 
may deem fit and proper in the interest of justice. 
 
Brief Facts of the Case 
2. The Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (“CIRP”) of M/s Compuage 
Infocom Limited was initiated by this Tribunal vide order dated 02.11.2023 
in C.P (IB) 329 of 2023 under Section 7 of the Code filed by Plus Plus 
Unified Engagement Services Private Limited (“Financial Creditor”) 
wherein the Mr. Arun Kapoor was appointed as the Interim Resolution 
Professional (“IRP”) of the Corporate Debtor.

claims from the creditors of the Corporate Debtor on or before 16.11.2023. 
Upon receipt of claims, the Committee of Creditors (“CoC”) of the 
Corporate Debtor was constituted, comprising of the following members, 
and its first meeting was held on 02.12.2023:

02.01.2024 with last date for submission of Expression of Interest by 
17.01.2024, which was extended till 16.02.2024.  
 
5. At the 5th meeting of the CoC held on 28.03.2024, the CoC approved, with 
a voting share of 85.72%, the replacement of the existing Resolution 
Professional, Mr. Arun Kapoor, with Mr. Gajesh Labhchand Jain. 
Accordingly, the CoC filed IA No. 1984 of 2024 which was allowed by 
this Tribunal vide order dated 29.04.2024, appointing the Applicant as the 
Resolution Professional of the Corporate Debtor. 
 
6. In response to the issuance of Form G, five resolution plans were received. 
The status of the plans received was placed before the CoC at its 6th 
meeting held on 22.04.2024. Thereafter, at the 7th meeting held on 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 8 of 18 
 
30.05.2024, the resolution plans were formally opened and subsequently 
circulated to the members of the CoC vide email dated 03.06.2024. 
 
7. In the 9th and 10th meetings of the CoC, held on 26.08.2024 and 19.09.2024, 
respectively, the Applicant apprised the CoC that, only NPL Bluesky 
Automotive Private Limited had furnished the requisite EMD and 
annexures in accordance with the RFRP, while three other PRAs had 
expressed their intention to withdraw.  
 
8. In the 11th meeting of the CoC held on 25.10.2024, the CoC, with a voting 
majority of 94.94%, approved the issuance of a fresh Form G, as the 
resolution plans received did not comply with the provisions of the Code. 
Accordingly, a fresh Form G was issued on 17.11.2024 (Annexure 8), 
including extending the last date for submission of EoIs from 03.12.2024 
to 13.12.2024 (Annexure 9). 
 
9. In the 13th meeting of the CoC held on 03.01.2025, the Applicant apprised 
the CoC that 19 EoIs had been received, of which 18 were found eligible 
for inclusion in the final list. Subsequently, in the 14th meeting held on 
27.02.2025, the Applicant informed the CoC that 14 resolution plans had 
been received, while the remaining 4 PRAs had not submitted their plans. 
 
10. In the 16th meeting of the CoC held on 30.04.2025, the CoC decided to 
invite revised resolution plans from the PRAs, excluding from their scope 
the inventory situated in India and Singapore, as well as the funds lying in 
India and at the Singapore branch, with 20.05.2025 fixed as the last date 
for submission. Accordingly, all fourteen PRAs submitted their revised 
plans by the stipulated date, which were opened and circulated to the CoC 
at its 17th meeting held on 27.05.2025. Thereafter, at its 18th meeting held 
on 19.06.2025, the CoC approved, with a voting share of 75.28%, the 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 9 of 18 
 
updated list of creditors incorporating claims received up to 16.06.2025, 
which was taken on record by this Tribunal in IA No. 4326 of 2025.  
 
11. In the 20th meeting of the CoC held on 14.08.2025, all fourteen revised 
resolution plans were placed for e-voting, which commenced on 
16.08.2025. At the request of the CoC members, the voting window was 
extended from time to time up to 14.11.2025, i.e., for 90 days. None of the 
plans received the approval of 66% of the voting share.  
 
12. In the same meeting, the proposal to liquidate the Corporate Debtor 
(Voting Item No. 12) was also put to e-voting. It received 43.16% votes 
in favour and 12.56% against, 1.08% abstained and 43.20% did not vote. 
The proposal, therefore, failed to secure the requisite 66% voting share. 
Consequently, the CoC did not approve the proposal for liquidation and 
failed to propose the name of the Liquidator of the Corporate Debtor. 
 
13. The 22nd meeting of the CoC was held on 15.11.2025 and, after 
adjournment, on 18.11.2025. The Applicant apprised the CoC that neither 
any resolution plan nor the proposal for liquidation had received the 
approval of 66% of the voting share, and placed three options before it, 
namely, to continue with the existing Form G, to issue a fresh Form G (both 
subject to a further extension of the CIRP period), or to file an application 
for liquidation under Section 33(1) of the Code. The minutes record that 
Indian Bank (31.45%) and Bandhan Bank (7.77%) requested the Applicant 
to apply for liquidation; Central Bank of India (29.02%) and Punjab 
National Bank (12.56%) preferred a fresh Form G; Tata Capital Limited 
(0.72%) stated that it would abide by the majority; and the other members 
did not communicate their positions.  
 
 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 10 of 18 
 
14. The last extension of the CIRP period was granted by this Tribunal vide 
order dated 12.01.2026, thereby extending the CIRP period up to 
20.11.2025, being the 750th day of the CIRP. 
 
15. As the Committee of Creditors failed to pass a resolution for liquidation 
with the requisite majority of 66% and consequently did not propose the 
appointment of any Liquidator, the Applicant being constrained to invoke 
Section 33(1) of the Code, has filed the present Application on 24.11.2025 
seeking an order for liquidation of the Corporate Debtor. 
 
Reply of Respondent No. 1 
16. Respondent No. 1, Indian Bank states that it is the Lead Bank of the 
consortium of lenders and the largest member of the CoC, holding a voting 
share of 31.45% and that it does not oppose the present Application. 
 
17. It is submitted that despite issuance of Form G twice, receipt of plans from 
14 Prospective Resolution Applicants and conduct of a challenge process, 
none of the resolution plans secured the requisite 66% voting share of the 
CoC. The proposal for liquidation also received only 43.16% votes in 
favour. 
 
18. It is further submitted that in the absence of an approved resolution plan 
within the maximum period prescribed under the Code, liquidation is 
warranted under Section 33(1)(a) of the Code, and any further extension 
would increase costs and prejudice the creditors. Accordingly, Respondent 
No. 1 has expressed no objection to the reliefs sought in the present 
Application. 
 
Reply of Respondent No. 15 
19. Respondent No. 15, Tata Capital Limited (“TCL”), has filed an Affidavit 
in Reply stating that TCL is the successor entity of Tata Capital Financial 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 11 of 18 
 
Services Limited pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by 
this Tribunal vide order dated 24.11.2023, with effect from 01.01.2024, 
and that all rights and obligations arising out of the financial facilities 
extended to the Corporate Debtor stood transferred to it. 
 
20. It is submitted that the Corporate Debtor had availed various Channel 
Finance facilities from it between 2014 and 2022 and had defaulted in 
repayment from March 2023. Its loan account was consequently classified 
as a Non-Performing Asset on 03.06.2023, following which TCL issued a 
Loan Recall Notice dated 26.06.2023 for an outstanding amount of Rs. 
4,23,55,515.70, along with applicable interest and charges. 
 
21. Respondent No. 15 further submits that pursuant to the commencement of 
CIRP vide order dated 02.11.2023, it submitted its claim in Form C for Rs. 
4.47 crore, which was admitted in full by the Resolution Professional, and 
it was accordingly recognised as an unsecured financial creditor of the 
Corporate Debtor with a voting share of 0.72% in the CoC. 
 
22. TCL states that despite repeated issuance of Form G and consideration of 
various resolution plans, none of the resolution plans received the requisite 
approval of 66% of the voting share of the CoC, even after extension of the 
voting period until 14.11.2025. TCL has further stated that, in the 22nd 
meeting of the CoC, it voted in favour of the proposal for liquidation of the 
Corporate Debtor and the appointment of the Applicant as Liquidator, as 
recorded in the minutes dated 18.11.2025. 
 
23. In view of the aforesaid submissions, TCL has expressed no objection to 
the reliefs sought in the present Application, and has supported the 
liquidation of the Corporate Debtor in accordance with the provisions of 
the Code, and prayed that the Application be allowed. 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 12 of 18 
 
 
Analysis and Findings 
24. We have heard the learned counsel for the Applicant and Respondent No. 
1, Respondent No. 2 and Respondent No. 15 and perused the material on 
record. 
 
25. At the outset, we observe that during the course of hearing on 27.10.2026, 
the following order was passed: 
 
1. This is the IA filed by the RP seeking liquidation of the 
Corporate Debtor. This matter had come up for our 
consideration on 01.09.2026, wherein one last and final 
opportunity was granted to the Respondents to file reply with 
a self-operative order that failing to file the reply shall lead to 
forfeiture of right to file reply and matter shall proceed 
accordingly. 
         2.  It is submitted to us that except Respondent No.1 and 
Respondent No.15, no one has filed reply. It is also submitted 
that Respondent No.1 and Respondent No.15 in their reply 
support the present liquidation application. 
3. Heard, Ld. Counsel for the Applicant, Counsel for the 
Respondent No.1, Respondent No.2 and Respondent No.15. 
The Respondent No.2 Central Bank of India opposes the 
liquidation in view of their IA bearing no. 711 of 2026. 
Accordingly, matter is reserved for orders. 
 
26. It is noted that despite being granted a final opportunity to file their 
respective replies, only Respondent Nos. 1 and 15 have filed their replies, 
both of whom have supported the present Application and expressed no 
objection to the liquidation of the Corporate Debtor. The remaining 
Respondents, including Respondent No. 2, Central Bank of India, have 
failed to file their replies within the time granted by this Adjudicating 
Authority. Accordingly, in terms of the order dated 01.09.2026, their right 
to file replies stood forfeited. 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 13 of 18 
 
 
27. It is further noted that the Applicant has approached this Adjudicating 
Authority seeking liquidation of the Corporate Debtor under Section 33(1) 
of the Code. In this regard, it is pertinent to refer to the relevant provisions 
of Section 33 of the Code, which deal with the initiation of liquidation 
proceedings. The same are reproduced below for ready reference: 
 
Section 33 - Initiation of liquidation 
 
(1) Where the Adjudicating Authority, — 
a) before the expiry of the insolvency resolution process period 
or the maximum period permitted for completion of the 
corporate insolvency resolution process under section 12 or 
the fast track corporate insolvency resolution process under 
section 56, as the case may be, does not receive a resolution 
plan under sub-section (6) of section 30; or 
b) rejects the resolution plan under section 31 for the non-
compliance of the requirements specified therein, 
it shall— 
(i) pass an order requiring the corporate debtor to be liquidated 
in the manner as laid down in this Chapter; 
(ii) issue a public announcement stating that the corporate debtor 
is in liquidation; and 
(iii)  require such order to be sent to the authority with which the 
corporate debtor is registered." 
 
(2) Where the resolution professional, at any time during the 
corporate insolvency resolution process but before 
confirmation of resolution plan, intimates the Adjudicating 
Authority of the decision of the committee of creditors 
approved by not less than sixty-six percent of the voting share 
to liquidate or dissolve the corporate debtor, the Adjudicating 
Authority shall pass a liquidation order as referred to in- sub-
clauses (i)(ii)(iii)(iv) and (v) of clause (b) of sub-section (1). 
 
Explanation – For the purposes of this sub-section, it is hereby 
declared that the committee of creditors may take the decision 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 14 of 18 
 
to liquidate the corporate debtor, any time after its constitution 
under sub-section (1) of section 21 and before the confirmation 
of the resolution plan, including at any time before the 
preparation of the information memorandum.” 
 
28. Section 33(1) provides that where the Adjudicating Authority does not 
receive a resolution plan before the expiry of the CIRP period or the 
maximum period permitted for completion of the CIRP, it shall pass an 
order for liquidation of the Corporate Debtor. Whereas Section 33(2) of the 
Code provides that, at any stage during the CIRP, but before the approval 
of a resolution plan by the Adjudicating Authority, the CoC may, in 
exercise of its commercial wisdom, pass a resolution to liquidate the 
Corporate Debtor by a vote of not less than 66% of the voting share. Upon 
such decision being communicated by the RP to the Adjudicating 
Authority, the Adjudicating Authority is required to pass a liquidation 
order. Thus, the existence of a CoC resolution with requisite majority, and 
the filing of the application “at any time during the CIRP”, are statutory 
preconditions for initiating liquidation under Section 33(2) of the Code. 
There is no such requirement of Section 33(1) of the Code. 
 
29. Having regard to the aforesaid provisions, it is necessary to examine the 
facts of the present case. It is noted that the CIRP of the Corporate Debtor 
commenced vide order dated 02.11.2023. During the CIRP, the Resolution 
Professional issued Form G on two occasions and several resolution plans 
were received and considered by the CoC. However, despite repeated 
deliberations none of the revised resolution plans received the requisite 
approval of 66% voting share of the CoC.  
 
30. It is further noted that the proposal for liquidation of the Corporate Debtor 
was also placed before the CoC for voting in the 20th meeting held on 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 15 of 18 
 
14.08.2025 but failed to secure the requisite majority, having received only 
43.16% votes in favour. Thereafter, in the 22nd meeting of the CoC held on 
15.11.2025 and 18.11.2025, the Resolution Professional apprised the 
members that neither any resolution plan nor the proposal for liquidation 
had secured the requisite voting share and placed various options before 
the CoC, including issuance of a fresh Form G or filing an application for 
liquidation. However, the members of the CoC remained divided on the 
proposed course of action, and no decision on any of the options was taken 
by the CoC.  
 
31. In view of the above, it is evident that despite repeated efforts and sufficient 
opportunities, the CIRP of the Corporate Debtor could not culminate in 
approval of any resolution plan within the permissible period i.e. till the 
expiry of extended CIRP Period on 20.11.2025 which was the 750th day 
from the insolvency commencement date of 02.11.2023. Accordingly, the 
provisions of Section 33(1)(a) of the Code are attracted, and the Applicant 
has rightly invoked the said provision seeking liquidation of the Corporate 
Debtor. 
 
32. As regards prayer (c), seeking condonation of delay of five days in filing 
the present Application, it is noted that the delay is minor in nature and has 
arisen in the course of filing the present Application seeking liquidation of 
the Corporate Debtor. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, 
the delay in filing the Application is hereby condoned. 
 
33. Additionally, during the hearing held on 27.10.2026, Respondent No. 2, 
Central Bank of India opposed the liquidation of the Corporate Debtor in 
view of I.A No. 711 of 2026. In this regard, we note that the said objection 
has been duly been considered by this Adjudicating Authority in I.A No. 
711 of 2026, which has been dismissed by a separate order. We further note 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 16 of 18 
 
that despite issuance of Form G on two occasions and receipt of 14 
resolution plans, none of the plans could secure the requisite majority of 
66% voting share of the CoC. Further, no resolution was passed for 
extension or continuation of the CIRP. In these circumstances considering 
the CIRP has already continued for a substantial period without yielding 
any resolution, we find no merit in the objection raised by Respondent No. 
2 so as to warrant any further continuation of the CIRP. 
 
34. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this 
Adjudicating Authority is of the considered view that the Corporate Debtor 
is liable to be liquidated under Section 33(1)(a) of the Code, and 
accordingly, liquidation proceedings deserve to be initiated in accordance 
with Chapter III of Part II of the Code. Accordingly, the Corporate Debtor 
is ordered to be liquidated and the consequential order is as follows:  
ORDER 
 
a. The Corporate Debtor, Compuage Infocom Limited having CIN 
number L99999MH1999PLC135914, CRN: 135914 is directed to be 
liquidated in accordance with the provisions of Chapter III of Part II of 
the Code and applicable regulations. Consequently, the Applicant/RP 
stands relieved subject to procedural/necessary compliances under 
Section 34(5) of the Code. 
b. We deem it appropriate to appoint an Insolvency Professional from the 
panel of Insolvency Professionals shared by the IBBI, as Liquidator in 
this case. Accordingly, Mr. Ashok Mittal bearing Registration No. 
IBBI/IPA-001/IP-P-02549/2021-2022/13889, having address at S-138, 
B Wing, Express Zone Mall, Western Express Highway Goregaon East, 
Mumbai Suburban, Maharashtra, 400063, having Email id: 
ashokmittal2020[at]gmail[dot]com having AFA valid upto 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 17 of 18 
 
31.12.2026, is hereby appointed to act as the Liquidator in terms of 
Section 34 of the Code.  
c. The Liquidator shall initiate the liquidation process as envisaged under 
Chapter III of Part II of the Code and the Liquidation Process 
Regulations applicable on the date of passing of this order. He shall take 
control of all the assets of Corporate Debtor and also continue or institute 
proceedings in respect of avoidance transactions or fraudulent or 
wrongful trading, if any, as per section 35(1)(l) of the Code. 
d. The Liquidator shall be entitled to a fee for conducting the liquidation 
proceedings, as approved by the CoC or in accordance with Regulation 
4 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Liquidation Process) 
Regulations, 2016, as applicable on the date of passing of this order, as 
the case may be. 
e. The Committee of Creditors constituted under section 21 shall continue 
to function during the liquidation process as per Regulation 8 of the IBBI 
(Liquidation Process) Regulations, 2016. 
f. A fresh moratorium shall commence in terms of provision of Section 
33(1)(iv) of the Code. 
g. The Liquidator shall issue public announcement stating that the 
Corporate Debtor is in liquidation. 
h. This Order shall be deemed to be a notice of discharge to the officers, 
employees and workmen of the Corporate Debtor. 
i. The Liquidator shall submit a Preliminary Report to the Adjudicating 
Authority within 30 days from the liquidation commencement date as 
per Regulation 13 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Liquidation 

I.A (Liq) 94 of 2025 
Page 18 of 18 
 
Process) Regulations, 2016. The Liquidator shall also submit progress 
reports as per Regulation 15 of the Liquidation Process Regulations. 
j. The Liquidator is hereby authorised to represent the Corporate Debtor 
before the Government Authorities, if required. Further, in terms of 
Section 35(1)(k) of the Code, the Liquidator is authorised to institute or 
defend any suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings, whether civil or 
criminal, in the name of or on behalf of the Corporate Debtor, including 
in respect of any pending proceedings, in accordance with the provisions 
of the Code and other applicable laws. 
k. Registry shall furnish a copy of this Order within seven days from the 
passing of this Order to the following: 
i. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India; 
ii. Regional Director (Western Region), Ministry of Corporate 
Affairs; 
iii. Registrar of Companies, Mumbai – I; 
iv. Official Liquidator attached to Bombay High Court; 
v. Erstwhile Resolution Professional, Mr. Gajesh Labchand 
Jain 
vi. Liquidator, Ashok Mittal. 
35.  Accordingly, the I.A. (LIQ.) No. 94 of 2025 is allowed in above terms and 
stands disposed of.  
 
    Sd/-         Sd/-
